Xiang Chong, nicknamed “Eight-Armed Nezha,” answered to the Earthly Flying Star and ranked sixty-fourth among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes. An infantry commander, he joined Liangshan with Li Gun and Fan Rui from Mount Mangdang. Born in Pei County, Xuzhou, he was strong and exceptionally brave, adept at handling flying shields and round shields. His usual round shield held twenty-four throwing knives, and he carried javelins behind his back. In battle he spun the shield like a windmill to protect his body while launching knives and javelins with lightning speed at enemies several paces away. His uncanny attacks swept aside resistance. With shield, knives, and spears all moving together, he seemed to possess eight arms, while his ferocity recalled Prince Nezha of legend, who had three heads and six arms and rode wind-and-fire wheels. The nickname Eight-Armed Nezha praised the variety of his techniques and speed of his movements.

He had long been close to Li Gun. Both were fugitives from the Xuzhou region who, after committing crimes and finding nowhere to stay, went to Mount Mangdang and joined Fan Rui, the sorcerous Demon King of Chaos. Fan Rui was chief and the two became his deputies. They occupied the mountain, gathered a forest band, and raided and robbed. Fan Rui could summon wind and rain, while Xiang Chong and Li Gun had exceptional shield, spear, throwing-knife, and javelin skills. Their combined strength won them such renown that they began to dream of annexing Liangshan Marsh, boasting that they would seize its stronghold. This provoked their conflict with Liangshan.

Hearing the three men's boast, Song Jiang mustered an army and personally marched against Mount Mangdang. Gongsun Sheng accompanied him, saying Fan Rui's unorthodox arts could be controlled by true magic. In battle, Xiang Chong and Li Gun led the charge, holding round shields and brandishing javelins as they rolled forward close to the ground like a whirlwind. They burst into Song Jiang's formation and drove left and right without resistance, nearly taking his life. Lu Fang and Guo Sheng saved him, thrusting out their paired painted halberds and fighting hard to block the attackers. Gongsun Sheng also secretly aided them with spells and concealed pits prepared in advance. Eager to display their courage and carried away by the fighting, Xiang Chong and Li Gun failed to watch the ground. Both fell into the pits with their shields. Hidden soldiers rushed them with hooks and ropes, captured them alive, and brought them before the command tent.

Admiring their ability, Song Jiang came out personally, sent the soldiers away, untied them, and helped them into the tent. He served wine, reassured them kindly, and explained his purpose of carrying out Heaven's justice and gathering worthy men, urging them to leave darkness for the light. The two were straightforward men. Grateful that he treated them with such kindness and courtesy instead of as prisoners, they bowed and willingly submitted. They volunteered to return to Mount Mangdang and persuade Fan Rui to join. There they recounted Song Jiang's generosity and loyalty and urged Fan Rui not to remain obsessed with magical rivalry. When Fan Rui later lost his duel with Gongsun Sheng, he recognized the superiority of the orthodox arts. Under the two friends' earnest persuasion, he led the entire Mount Mangdang force into Liangshan's ranks. The three joined the marsh together and never separated again.

At the great ranking, Xiang Chong took the sixty-fourth seat as the Earthly Flying Star, serving as an infantry commander beside Li Gun. Their round shields and throwing knives were ideally suited to charging formations and leading assaults. In the hardest battles they usually entered first and threw enemy lines into confusion, an irresistible pair of infantry vanguards. During the subsequent campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, Xiang Chong repeatedly fought at the front and earned merit.

The Jiangnan campaign against Fang La brought the greatest danger. As the army reached the Shezhou region, Xiang Chong and Li Gun again led their troops into the enemy formation. They unexpectedly entered an ambush in treacherous terrain. Caught unprepared, they could not fully use their shields and were surrounded in the confused battle. Xiang Chong fought without retreat but was finally killed beneath many blades. The Eight-Armed Nezha, who had spent half a lifetime whirling his shield and throwing knives against every foe, lost his wings among Jiangnan's mountains. He and his dear friend Li Gun fell one after the other on the same day, never seeing the army's return. His loyal courage and terrible end form one of the most stirring passages in Water Margin's many heroic laments, leaving later readers to mourn his loss.
项充，绰号「八臂哪吒」，应地煞地飞星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十四位好汉，位列步.ja:
項充は「八臂哪吒」の異名を持ち、地煞の地飛星に応じる、梁山泊百八将の第六十四位の好漢である。歩軍頭領に列し、李袞、樊瑞とともに芒碭山の一隊から梁山へ帰順した。徐州沛県の出身で、体は強健、勇猛さは並外れ、飛牌や団牌を扱う名手だった。常用する丸盾には二十四本の飛刀を差し、背には投槍も隠していた。戦場では盾を風車のように舞わせて全身を守り、電光石火の間に槍や刀を投げて数歩先の敵を傷つけた。まさに神出鬼没で、立ち塞がる者をなぎ倒した。盾が翻り、刀槍が同時に動く様子は八本の腕があるようで、三頭六臂、風火輪に乗る神話の哪吒太子のように勇猛だったため、「八臂哪吒」と呼ばれた。手段の多さと動作の速さを称える名である。

項充はもとから李袞と親しかった。二人とも徐州一帯の命知らずで、罪を犯して居場所を失い、芒碭山へ向かって、妖術を使う混世魔王樊瑞と一党を成した。樊瑞が首領、項充と李袞が副将となり、三人は山を占め、仲間を集め、家々を襲って略奪した。樊瑞には風雨を呼ぶ術があり、二人には盾や槍を舞わせ、飛刀や投槍を放つ絶技があった。合力した威勢は赫々として、ついには梁山泊を併呑する野心を抱き、水滸の基盤を奪うと公言し、梁山との争いを起こした。

三人の大言を聞いた宋江は兵馬を集め、自ら芒碭山を征した。同行した公孫勝は、樊瑞の学んだものは邪道にすぎず、正法で制せると述べた。両軍が対陣すると、項充と李袞が先頭に立ち、団牌を構え、投槍を舞わせ、地を転がるように旋風の勢いで宋江の陣へ入った。左右に突き進む勢いを止める者はなく、宋公明は命を傷つけられかけた。呂方と郭盛が方天画戟をそろえて出し、必死に防いだうえ、公孫勝も密かに術で助け、あらかじめ落とし穴の仕掛けを設けていた。勇み立って戦いに夢中になった二人は足元を警戒せず、盾もろとも穴に落ちた。伏兵が一斉に押し寄せ、鉤と縄で生け捕りにし、陣幕の前へ送った。

二人の英雄ぶりを認めた宋江は、自ら幕を出て兵を退かせ、縄を解き、手を添えて幕内へ招いた。酒を振る舞って優しく慰め、天に代わって道を行い、賢者を集める志を語り、暗きを捨て明に投ずるよう勧めた。率直な二人は、捕虜としてではなく礼を尽くして遇される仁義に感謝し、ひれ伏して帰順した。さらに芒碭山へ帰って樊瑞を説得すると申し出た。山では宋公明の恩徳と義気を詳しく語り、術を競って覇を争うことに執着するなと諭した。その後、樊瑞は公孫勝との術比べに敗れ、正道の強さを知った。項充と李袞の懸命な説得を受け、芒碭山の全軍を率いて梁山へ帰順した。三人は共に水滸へ入り、再び離れることはなかった。

聚義の席次では、項充は地飛星、第六十四位に列し、李袞と肩を並べる歩軍頭領となった。二人は団牌と飛刀を使い慣れ、敵陣へ突入し、先駆けて突破するのに最も適していた。激しい難戦ではたびたび最初に入り、敵の陣をかき乱す、梁山歩軍の鋭く止め難い先鋒の一組だった。その後の遼国、田虎、王慶の征討でも、項充は先頭で戦い、軍功を立てた。

方臘征討の江南の戦いは、最も危険だった。軍が歙州一帯へ進むと、項充と李袞はいつものように兵を率いて先陣を切ったが、思いがけず伏兵にはまった。険悪な地形で不意を突かれ、優れた団牌も十分使えず、乱軍の重囲へ陥った。項充は力戦して退かなかったが、ついに無数の刃の下で殺され、戦場に命を落とした。半生、盾を舞わせ飛刀を放ち、行く手を阻まれなかった「八臂哪吒」も、江南の山々で翼を折られた。親友李袞と同じ日に相次いで命を捧げ、凱旋の日を見ることはなかった。その忠勇と凄惨な結末は、水滸の多くの英雄の悲歌の中でもとりわけ壮烈な一筆であり、後人を無念に嘆かせるのである。
项充，绰号「八臂哪吒」，应地煞地飞星，乃梁山泊一百单八将中第六十四位好汉，位列步.zh_TW:
項充，綽號「八臂哪吒」，應地煞地飛星，乃梁山泊一百單八將中第六十四位好漢，位列步軍頭領，與李袞、樊瑞同自芒碭山一支歸順梁山。項充乃徐州沛縣人氏，生得身強體健，驍勇絕倫，是個使飛牌、弄團牌的好手。其人慣使一面團牌，牌上插著二十四把飛刀，背後又藏標槍，臨陣之際，手舞團牌如風車一般，護住渾身，又能於電光石火之間飛出標槍、擲出飛刀，傷人於數步之外，端的神出鬼沒，擋者披靡。江湖中人見他臨陣時團牌翻飛、刀槍並舉，恍如有八條臂膊一齊使將出來，又勇悍如神話中那三頭六臂、腳踏風火輪的哪吒太子，故送他這「八臂哪吒」的諢號，極言其手段之繁、動作之疾。

項充原與李袞交厚，二人皆是徐州一帶的亡命之徒，因犯了事，無處安身，遂投奔芒碭山，與那會行妖法的混世魔王樊瑞結為一夥。樊瑞居首，項充、李袞為其副將，三人盤踞芒碭，嘯聚山林，打家劫舍。樊瑞既有呼風喚雨之術，項充、李袞又各挾一身舞牌弄槍、飛刀擲標的絕技，三人合勢，聲威赫赫，竟生出吞併梁山泊的野心，揚言要來奪這水滸基業，因此與梁山結下爭端。

宋江聞得芒碭山三人狂言，便點起軍馬，親征芒碭。公孫勝隨行，謂樊瑞所習不過左道，自有正法可制。兩軍對陣，項充、李袞當先出馬，各挺團牌、舞動標槍，滾地而來，勢如旋風，殺入宋江陣中，左衝右突，無人能擋，險些傷了宋公明性命。虧得呂方、郭盛兩員副將，使方天畫戟雙戟齊出，奮力遮攔，又得公孫勝暗中作法相助，先佈下陷坑機關。項充、李袞逞勇直前，殺得性起，不防腳下，連人帶牌一齊跌入陷坑之中，被埋伏的軍士一擁而上，撓鉤套索，生擒活捉，押到帳前。

宋江見二人英雄了得，親自下帳，喝退軍士，解其繩縛，扶入帳中，置酒相待，好言撫慰，說自家替天行道、招賢納士之意，勸二人棄暗投明。項充、李袞本是直性漢子，見宋江如此仁義、不以俘虜相待，反以禮遇，心下感激，納頭便拜，情願歸順。二人又自請回芒碭山去，說樊瑞來降。果然回山之後，備說宋公明的恩德義氣，又勸樊瑞莫要執迷於鬥法爭雄。其後樊瑞與公孫勝鬥法不勝，方知正道高強，遂在項、李二人苦勸之下，率領芒碭山一應人馬，盡數歸順梁山。三人自此同歸水滸，再不分離。

聚義排座次，項充列地飛星，居第六十四位，與李袞並肩，同為步軍頭領。二人慣使團牌飛刀，最宜衝鋒陷陣、破敵先登，凡有惡戰硬仗，每每當先突入，專一衝亂敵陣，是梁山步軍中一對銳不可當的先鋒。其後隨大軍南征北討，徵遼國、平田虎、定王慶，項充皆衝殺在前，立下戰功。

及至征討方臘，江南一役最為兇險。其時大軍徵進至歙州一帶，項充、李袞二人依舊當先突陣，引兵衝殺。不料中了敵軍埋伏，地形險惡，二人措手不及，團牌雖利，卻難施展，竟陷於亂軍重圍之中。項充力戰不退，終於亂刀之下身遭殺害，殞命疆場。可憐一員「八臂哪吒」，半世舞牌飛刀、所向無前，到頭來折翼於江南山嶺，與摯友李袞先後同日捐軀，未能見班師之日。其忠勇之概、慘烈之結局，亦水滸眾多英雄悲歌中至為壯烈的一筆，令後人讀之，無不為之扼腕。

萧让，济州人氏，乃一介读书的秀士。其人饱读诗书，写得一手好字，真草隶篆四般书法无.en:
Xiao Rang, a native of Jizhou, was a learned scholar. Widely read in poetry and the classics, he excelled in all four calligraphic styles: regular, cursive, clerical, and seal script. He was especially skilled at imitating famous hands from past and present, producing copies almost indistinguishable from the originals. This earned him the elegant nickname “Sacred-Handed Scholar.” A physically frail man of letters, he originally earned his living in Jizhou teaching pupils and writing for others. He was a close friend of Jin Dajian, the Jade-Armed Craftsman, who excelled at engraving inscriptions and seals. One wrote and the other carved, making them a perfect pair. Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, Xiao Rang answered to the Earthly Literary Star and held the forty-sixth seat. As a civil officer, he handled official correspondence, proclamations, and written troop assignments.

His recruitment arose from Song Jiang's rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower and Wu Yong's ensuing scheme. After Song Jiang drunkenly wrote the poem on the tower wall, the assistant prefect Huang Wenbing denounced him. Prefect Cai Jiu placed him on death row and sent a letter to the Eastern Capital, seeking to have him transferred there for judgment. Eager to rescue him, Wu Yong planned to forge a reply from Cai Jing, induce the authorities to escort Song Jiang to the capital, and free him on the road. But forging the grand preceptor's letter required someone who could imitate his handwriting and someone who could carve his seal. Wu Yong recommended two outstanding men of Jizhou to Chao Gai: Xiao Rang, who could reproduce many calligraphic hands, and Jin Dajian, who could carve every kind of seal.

Liangshan sent men to lure them out of the city. Claiming that the Sacred Peak Temple in Tai'anzhou needed a stele inscription and written petitions, the messengers offered generous payment. Xiao Rang and Jin Dajian unsuspectingly agreed to go. Halfway there, Lin Chong, Dai Zong, and other heroes appeared and openly invited them to the mountain. Seeing no escape and hearing of Liangshan's loyalty, the two went up and joined. Under Wu Yong's direction, Xiao Rang imitated Cai Jing's handwriting to produce the reply, and Jin Dajian carved and stamped his seal. But they overlooked a crucial detail: a letter between Cai Jing and his son Cai Jiu should not bear a seal reading “Hanlin Cai Jing.” Huang Wenbing saw the mistake immediately and exposed the forgery. Song Jiang and Dai Zong nearly died as a result; only Liangshan's raid on the execution ground and upheaval in Jiangzhou saved them. Though this scheme briefly backfired, the two men's writing and engraving skills became valued assets at Liangshan.

Xiao Rang then took charge of literary work. Most of Liangshan's letters, public announcements, and deployment orders came from his hand, and his fine calligraphy lent distinction to the stronghold. At the great ranking he joined the Earthly Stars as the Literary Star, handling records with Jin Dajian and the other civil officers. Though he did not fight at the front, he was indispensable to the stronghold's planning and written administration.

After the amnesty, he accompanied Song Jiang's army against Great Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing, and Fang La in Jiangnan. Throughout these campaigns he managed documents rather than exposing himself directly to arrows and stones. The bloody Jiangnan fighting left the Liangshan heroes dead and wounded in great numbers, but his civil duties spared his life, and he was among those who returned from the southern expedition. When rewards were assigned, his unrivaled calligraphy had made his name in the capital. Grand Preceptor Cai Jing admired him and kept him in the Eastern Capital as a resident tutor in his household, chiefly writing for him. Xiao Rang thus lived comfortably in the capital for the rest of his life and met a peaceful end. From writing for hire to outlawry at Liangshan, then back into lawful imperial service, the scholar preserved his life through his fine brushwork, a rare fortunate outcome among so many heroes killed in battle. His calligraphy and literary ability are still praised by later generations.
萧让，济州人氏，乃一介读书的秀士。其人饱读诗书，写得一手好字，真草隶篆四般书法无.ja:
蕭譲は済州の出身で、学問を修めた秀士だった。詩書をよく読み、真・草・隷・篆の四体すべてに精通する能筆で、とりわけ古今の名家の筆跡をまねることに優れた。臨書は真作とほとんど見分けがつかず、江湖では「聖手書生」という雅号を贈られた。もとは文弱の書生で、済州城内で生徒を教え、人の代筆をして暮らしていた。金石の文字や印を彫る名手、玉臂匠金大堅と親しく、一人が書き、一人が彫る、絶好の組み合わせだった。梁山泊百八人では地文星に応じ、第四十六位に座した。行文や檄文、兵の配置命令を専門に掌る文職頭領である。

梁山入りは、宋江が潯陽楼に反詩を書いた事件と、呉用の計略に由来する。酔った宋江が楼の壁に反詩を書くと、通判黄文炳に告発され、蔡九知府は死囚牢へ入れた。さらに東京へ書状を送り、都へ護送して罪を問おうとした。救出を急ぐ梁山で呉用は蔡京の返信を偽造し、宋江を上京の護送へ出させ、途中で奪還する策を考えた。しかし太師の書状を偽るには、筆跡をまねる者と印を彫る者が必要だった。そこで済州の二人の名手、諸家の字体を書ける聖手書生蕭譲と、さまざまな印を彫れる玉臂匠金大堅を晁蓋に推薦した。

梁山は人を下山させ、計略で二人を城外へ誘い出した。使者は泰安州の岳廟で碑文を彫り、疏文を書く仕事があると偽り、高額の礼を約束した。蕭譲と金大堅は疑わず喜んで同行したが、道半ばで林冲、戴宗らが現れ、山へ招きたいと明かした。逃れられず、また梁山の義気を聞いた二人は入山し、仲間となった。呉用の指図で蕭譲は蔡京の筆跡をまねて返信を作り、金大堅が彫った蔡京の印を押した。ところが見落としがあった。蔡京から息子の蔡九への手紙に「翰林蔡京」の四字の印を使うべきではなかったのである。黄文炳は一目で偽書と見破り、宋江と戴宗はそろって殺されかけた。幸い梁山の好漢が刑場を襲い、江州を騒がせて救出した。二人の技巧は一時裏目に出たものの、書と彫刻の才は以後梁山で重んじられた。

入山後の蕭譲は文墨を専ら担当した。梁山が交わす書簡、布告、調遣の命令の多くは彼の手になり、美しい書は山寨の面目を高めた。大聚義では地煞の文星に列し、金大堅ら文職頭領とともに文書を扱った。陣前で戦うことはなくても、山寨の運営や行文に欠かせない人物だった。

招安後は宋江の大軍に従い、大遼を破り、田虎、王慶を平定し、江南の方臘征討に至るまで各地を転戦した。常に軍中の文書を掌り、自ら矢石を冒すことはなかった。江南の血戦では梁山の好漢の死傷が重なったが、文職であったため幸い命を保ち、南征から生還した者に名を連ねた。戦功への褒賞が行われる頃、その当代随一の書は都にも名高く、蔡京太師に認められた。東京に留められて屋敷の門館先生となり、専ら蔡太師のために字を書き、以後都で安らかに余年を楽しみ、よい最期を得た。人の代筆をする書生から梁山の山賊となり、再び帰順して朝廷へ戻り、一本の優れた筆で身命を全うしたのである。多くの好漢が戦場に死んだ梁山にあって、まれな幸運な結末であり、その書法と文墨の才は今も後人に称えられている。
萧让，济州人氏，乃一介读书的秀士。其人饱读诗书，写得一手好字，真草隶篆四般书法无.zh_TW:
蕭讓，濟州人氏，乃一介讀書的秀士。其人飽讀詩書，寫得一手好字，真草隸篆四般書法無所不精，尤善摹仿古今名家筆跡，所臨之字以假亂真，幾不可辨，故江湖上送他一個雅號，喚作「聖手書生」。蕭讓本是個文弱書生，原在濟州城中以教授生徒、代人書寫為業，與玉臂匠金大堅相交甚厚。金大堅善刻金石圖書印記，二人一書一刻，恰是一對絕配。在梁山泊一百單八人之中，蕭讓上應地文星，坐第四十六把交椅，專一掌管行文走檄、調兵差撥之事，乃梁山文職頭領。

蕭讓上梁山，緣於宋江潯陽樓題反詩、吳用智賺一節。話說宋江因醉酒在潯陽樓壁上題了反詩，被通判黃文炳告發，蔡九知府將宋江下了死牢，又遣人齎書往東京，欲解宋江赴京問罪。梁山好漢聞知，急要救人，吳用心生一計，欲偽造一封蔡京回書，賺得宋江押解上京，途中劫了。然偽造太師書信，須得有人能摹蔡京筆跡、刻蔡京印信方可。吳用遂向晁蓋薦舉濟州兩個絕妙之人：一個便是寫得諸家字型的聖手書生蕭讓，一個便是雕得諸般印記的玉臂匠金大堅。

於是梁山差人下山，用計賺蕭讓、金大堅出城。來人詐稱泰安州岳廟要刻碑文、寫疏頭，重金相聘，蕭讓、金大堅不疑，欣然隨往。行至半路，林沖、戴宗等一眾好漢殺出，明言相請上山。蕭讓、金大堅見走脫不得，又聞梁山義氣，遂上了山寨，入了大夥。當下吳用主謀，蕭讓摹仿蔡京字型，偽造回書一封；金大堅雕成蔡京印章，鈐於書上。豈料事有疏漏，蔡京與子蔡九父子之間，印記本不當用「翰林蔡京」四字圖書，黃文炳一眼看破，識出書信是偽，宋江、戴宗險些因此同遭殺身之禍，幸得梁山好漢劫了法場，大鬧江州，方救出二人。蕭讓、金大堅雖一時弄巧成拙，然其書刻之能，自此為梁山所重。

蕭讓既入梁山，便專掌文墨。凡梁山往來書札、曉諭文告、調遣號令，多出其手；其書法之妙，亦每為山寨壯色。梁山大聚義排定座次，蕭讓位列地煞文星，與金大堅等文職頭領同司案牘，雖不臨陣廝殺，卻是山寨運籌行文不可或缺之人。

朝廷招安之後，蕭讓隨宋江大軍，先破大遼，復平田虎、王慶，及至征討江南方臘，轉戰四方，皆在軍中掌管文書，未嘗親冒矢石。江南血戰，梁山好漢死傷枕藉，蕭讓以文職之故，幸得保全性命，南征還師，名列存者之中。其後論功行賞，因蕭讓書法冠絕當世，名動京華，竟為蔡京蔡太師所賞識，留在東京，充作府中門館先生，專一替蔡太師寫字，從此寓居京師，安享餘年，得了個善終。一介書生，自代人書寫而落草梁山，自落草而歸正還朝，終以一筆好字保身全命，於梁山眾多殞命疆場的好漢之中，可謂難得的善果。其人書法之精、文墨之能，至今猶為後人所稱道。

解宝，登州人氏，与兄解珍同为登州城外猎户出身，乃解珍之亲弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山乡.en:
Xie Bao was a native of Dengzhou and the younger brother of Xie Zhen. Both came from a hunting family outside the city. Their people had lived in Dengzhou's mountain country for generations, and the brothers had followed their elders into the forests from childhood, learning to take tigers and other beasts. They used all-iron, steel-pointed hunting forks and were skilled at setting spring bows and poisoned arrows; many local tigers and leopards fell to them. Strongly built and fiercely courageous, Xie Bao was as resolute as his brother. He was called the “Twin-Tailed Scorpion,” while Xie Zhen was the Two-Headed Snake. Both nicknames came from venomous creatures, suggesting men who were dangerous to provoke and would wound at a touch, while reflecting their hunters' boldness.

His everyday dress matched his brother's: an animal hide over his shoulders, a sharp blade at his waist, and a steel fork in his hand as he moved through Dengzhou's deep mountains and dense forests. Two flying yakshas tattooed on his legs added to his fierce appearance. Throughout the region, everyone knew the Xie brothers as formidable hunters.

Their arrival at Liangshan began with a grave injustice over a tiger hunt. A white-browed tiger with slanting eyes was killing people in Dengzhou's mountains, and the prefect ordered the local hunters to destroy it within a fixed time. Taking the official order, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao went into the hills and set spring bows with poisoned arrows. They hit the tiger, but it rolled down the slope and fell into the rear garden of Old Master Mao's estate. When the brothers demanded its body, Mao coveted the official credit and reward. He denied their claim and instead accused them of committing robbery and violence at his home in broad daylight. His son Mao Zhongyi colluded with Dengzhou's military commandant and bribed the authorities. The brothers were arrested, tortured into false confessions, and placed on death row, with their enemies determined to kill them.

Wrongly imprisoned, they were near death. Fortunately, their cousin Gu Dasao, the Tigress, kept a tavern in Dengzhou. Fierce and chivalrous, she valued family ties above all. Hearing of their plight, she planned a prison rescue with her husband Sun Xin, the Little Yuchi. They also enlisted his elder brother Sun Li, the Sick Yuchi and Dengzhou's military commander, the uncle and nephew Zou Yuan the Forest-Emerging Dragon and Zou Run the Single-Horned Dragon, Yue He the Iron Whistle, and other heroes. Acting together, they broke into Dengzhou's prison, rescued the Xie brothers, and killed the entire Mao household to avenge the injustice.

With nowhere to stay after the prison raid, the heroes agreed to join Liangshan. Its forces were then stalled in their three attacks on Zhu Family Village. Sun Li had studied under the same master as the village's martial instructor Luan Tingyu, so he devised a false-surrender plan. He led the group into the village to act as insiders. Xie Bao entered with Xie Zhen, Sun Li, Gu Dasao, and the others. When Liangshan attacked, they turned on the defenders and coordinated with the army outside, crushing Zhu Family Village. Xie Bao fought bravely and earned merit, then went up to Liangshan with the rest and became a commander.

At the great assembly he joined the Heavenly Stars, ranking thirty-fifth as the Heavenly Weeping Star. He and Xie Zhen both served as infantry commanders. Their hunting background made them experts at climbing mountains, laying ambushes, and shooting game. Whenever a campaign brought forests, dangerous passes, or steep ground that had to be climbed, the brothers were commonly sent first. They both served in the attacks on Zengtou Town, Dongping, and Dongchang.

After the amnesty, Xie Bao fought against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, never shrinking from campaigns north and south. In the Fang La expedition, the army reached Black Dragon Ridge, whose pass stood atop a sheer and treacherous cliff. Confident in their hunters' climbing skills, the brothers volunteered to scale the ridge at night and raid the stronghold. They climbed vines and creepers up the rock face, but Fang La's guards discovered them. Logs and stones were rolled down from above, and hooks were used against the climbers. Exhausted, Xie Zhen lost his grip and fell with his fork into a deep ravine, dying in the fall. Xie Bao was attacked below the ridge by a mass of arrows, spears, and halberds and died amid the enemy troops. Both gave their lives at Black Dragon Ridge on the same day. From the wrongful tiger case in Dengzhou's forests to their deaths for the country on a Jiangnan cliff, the Twin-Tailed Scorpion and his brother shared hardship, life, and death without abandoning each other. True to the name Heavenly Weeping Star, the brothers' joint fall moved all who heard it to tears, one of the most poignant endings of loyalty and courage among Water Margin's heroes.
解宝，登州人氏，与兄解珍同为登州城外猎户出身，乃解珍之亲弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山乡.ja:
解宝は登州の出身で、兄の解珍と同じく城外の猟師の家に生まれた実弟である。解氏は代々登州の山里に住み、狩りを生業としていた。兄弟は幼い頃から父たちと山林へ入り、虎や獣を捕らえる優れた技を学んだ。総鉄の鋼先の叉を使い、仕掛け弓や毒矢にも巧みで、登州の虎豹の多くがその手に倒れた。解宝は頑健な体に激しい勇気を備え、兄と同じく剛烈で果断だったため、江湖で「双尾蝎」と呼ばれた。兄の解珍は「両頭蛇」で、二人の異名はいずれも毒を持つ生き物に由来する。触れれば傷つけられる凶猛さと、猟師としての勇悍な本性を表していた。

日頃の装束も兄と変わらず、獣皮をまとい、腰に鋭い刃を下げ、鋼叉を手にして、登州の深山密林に出没した。両脚には飛天夜叉を二つ彫っており、いっそう凶悍な姿を見せた。登州一帯で解氏兄弟といえば、山中の手強い名猟師として知らぬ者はなかった。

梁山入りは、虎狩りをめぐる大きな冤罪に始まった。登州の山に、吊り目で白い額の虎が現れて人を傷つけたため、知府は管内の猟師に期限を切って捕殺を命じた。解珍と解宝は公文書を受け、山に仕掛け弓と毒矢を設け、虎を射た。ところが虎は矢を受けて斜面を転がり、麓の毛太公の荘園の裏庭へ落ちた。兄弟が虎の死骸を返すよう求めると、毛太公は役所から手柄と賞金を得ようと欲を出し、知らぬふりをしたうえ、白昼に押し入って強盗と暴行を働いたと逆に訴えた。息子の毛仲義も登州の兵馬都監と結託して役所を買収し、兄弟を捕らえて拷問で虚偽の自白をさせ、死囚牢へ入れ、どうしても殺そうとした。

無実のまま投獄された兄弟の命は危うかった。幸い従姉の顧大嫂は登州城内で居酒屋を開いていた。「母大虫」と呼ばれる激しく侠気ある女で、骨肉の情を何より重んじた。従弟の冤罪を知ると、夫の「小尉遅」孫新と牢破りを相談した。さらに孫新の兄で登州兵馬提轄の「病尉遅」孫立、「出林竜」鄒淵と「独角竜」鄒潤の叔父甥、「鉄叫子」楽和らを招いた。皆が心を合わせて登州の牢を破り、解珍と解宝を救い、毛太公の一家を殺して冤罪の恨みを晴らした。

牢破りの後は居場所がなくなり、好漢たちは共に梁山へ向かうことを約した。当時、梁山は三度の祝家荘攻めで行き詰まっていた。孫立は祝家荘の教師欒廷玉と同門だったため、偽降して一行を荘内に入れ、内応する策を立てた。解宝も兄や孫立、顧大嫂らと入り込み、梁山の大軍が攻めると内外から呼応し、武器を返して祝家荘を大破した。解宝は勇敢に働いて戦功を立て、その後皆と山へ上り、頭領となった。

大聚義で解宝は天罡に列し、天哭星、第三十五位となり、解珍とともに歩軍頭領を務めた。もとが猟師なので、山を登り、伏兵を設け、獲物を射ることを最も得意とした。梁山の征戦で山林の険しい隘路や登攀を要する場所があれば、兄弟を先頭に使うことが多かった。曾頭市、東平、東昌の攻略などでも、二人は力を尽くした。

招安後は遼国、田虎、王慶を征し、南北の戦いで一度も退かなかった。方臘征討で大軍が烏竜嶺へ来ると、関所は絶壁の頂に高く据えられ、地勢は険悪だった。解珍と解宝は猟師として断崖を登り慣れていることを頼みに、夜に嶺を登って寨を奇襲すると進んで願い出た。蔓や葛にすがって崖を上ったが、守備兵に気づかれ、上から丸太や石を落とされ、鉤でも狙われた。解珍は崖で力尽きて手を滑らせ、叉もろとも深い谷へ落ちて死んだ。解宝も嶺の下で矢や槍戟の集中攻撃を受け、乱軍の中で命を落とし、二人は同じ日に烏竜嶺の下で殉じた。「双尾蝎」解宝は兄と生死と苦難を共にし、登州の山林の虎事件で冤罪を受けてから、江南の絶壁で国に殉じるまで、決して離れなかった。「天哭星」の名に応じるように、兄弟そろっての戦死を聞く者は皆悲しみ泣いた。水滸の群雄の中でも涙を誘う、忠勇の結末である。
解宝，登州人氏，与兄解珍同为登州城外猎户出身，乃解珍之亲弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山乡.zh_TW:
解寶，登州人氏，與兄解珍同為登州城外獵戶出身，乃解珍之親弟。解氏兄弟世居登州山鄉，以打獵為生，自幼便隨父輩出入山林，習得一身擒虎捕獸的好本事，慣使渾鐵點鋼叉，又善設窩弓藥箭，登州山間虎豹，多喪其手。解寶生得身材壯健，性情狠勇，與兄解珍一般剛烈果決，江湖上送他一個綽號，喚作「雙尾蠍」。其兄解珍綽號「兩頭蛇」，兄弟二人綽號皆取自世間毒物，一蛇一蠍，蓋言其兇狠難惹、觸之即傷，亦顯二人獵戶行當的悍勇本色。

解寶平日裝束，與兄無異：身披獸皮，腰懸利刃，手提鋼叉，出沒於登州深山密林之間。他在兩腿上刺著兩個飛天夜叉，更顯其兇悍模樣，登州一帶提起解氏兄弟，無不知是山中一對厲害的好獵手。

解氏兄弟之上梁山，緣起於一樁獵虎奇冤。登州山中有一隻吊睛白額大蟲，傷害人命，知府限令本管獵戶限期捕殺。解珍、解寶領了公文，上山下了窩弓藥箭，射中那大蟲。豈料大蟲中箭滾下山坡，跌入山下毛太公莊院的後園裡去了。解氏兄弟下山討要虎屍，那毛太公貪圖虎屍可去官府請功領賞，竟昧心賴賬，反誣解珍、解寶白晝搶劫、上門行兇。毛太公之子毛仲義又與登州兵馬都監勾結，買通官府，將解珍、解寶拿去，屈打成招，下了死囚牢，必欲置之死地。

解氏兄弟含冤入獄，性命垂危。幸有表姐顧大嫂，綽號「母大蟲」，在登州城裡開酒店，潑辣豪俠，最重骨肉之情。顧大嫂聞知表弟蒙冤，便與丈夫「小尉遲」孫新商議劫牢救人，又請來孫新之兄、登州兵馬提轄「病尉遲」孫立，並「出林龍」鄒淵、「獨角龍」鄒潤叔侄、「鐵叫子」樂和等一干好漢，眾人同心，劫了登州大牢，救出解珍、解寶，殺了毛太公滿門，報了這場奇冤。

劫牢之後，眾好漢無處容身，遂相約同投梁山。其時梁山正三打祝家莊受阻，孫立舊與祝家莊教師欒廷玉是同窗師兄弟，便設下詐降之計，引一行人假投祝家莊做內應。解寶隨兄解珍並孫立、顧大嫂等混入莊中，待梁山大軍攻打之時，裡應外合，反戈相向，大破祝家莊。解寶在此役奮勇出力，立下戰功，自此隨眾上了梁山，做了山寨頭領。

梁山大聚義，解寶位列天罡，應天哭星，排第三十五位，與兄解珍同掌步軍頭領之職。二人本是獵戶，最善山地攀爬、設伏射獵，凡梁山征戰遇著山林險隘、需登高涉險之處，多用解氏兄弟當先。攻曾頭市、打東平東昌諸役，兄弟二人皆有效力。

招安之後，解寶隨大軍徵遼國，又徵田虎、王慶，南征北戰，未嘗退縮。及至征討方臘，大軍兵臨烏龍嶺。烏龍嶺關隘高踞絕壁之巔，地勢險惡，解珍、解寶自恃獵戶出身、慣能攀緣峭壁，遂主動請命，乘夜攀嶺去偷襲關寨。兄弟二人攀藤附葛，緣崖而上，不料被守嶺的方臘軍士察覺，嶺上推下檑木亂石，又用撓鉤搭人。解珍在崖壁上力竭失手，連人帶叉跌入深澗摔死；解寶在嶺下也被亂箭槍戟攢射，死於亂軍之中，兄弟二人同日捐軀於烏龍嶺下。這「雙尾蠍」解寶，與兄解珍同生死、共患難，自登州山林一樁虎案蒙冤起，至江南烏龍嶺一面峭壁殉國終，始終不離不棄。應著那「天哭星」的星名，兄弟雙雙戰死，聞者無不為之悲泣，實乃水滸群雄中一段令人垂淚的忠勇結局。

施恩者，孟州人氏也，乃管营之子。其父在孟州牢城营做管营之职，掌管一营囚徒，施恩便.en:
Shi En was a native of Mengzhou and the son of a prison camp superintendent. His father commanded the convicts at the Mengzhou penal camp, and Shi En used that small measure of authority to run a wine and meat shop in Happy Grove, east of the city. He also took a share of the proceeds from passing merchants, gambling houses and brothels, making himself a local strongman. From childhood he had practiced spear and staff and learned several styles of boxing and kicking. His yellow-toned complexion, keen eyes and somewhat chivalrous manner earned him the nickname Golden-Eyed Leopard. In this name, biao denotes a young tiger and conveys his tiger-like courage, while “golden-eyed” describes the piercing brightness of his gaze. Together they suggest that this young superintendent's son was no idle dandy, but a bold, strong man ready to compete and fight.

Shi En's fame arose entirely from the affair at Happy Grove. This busy crossroads east of Mengzhou drew merchants and travelers from every direction, with a hundred or so shops, gambling dens and money changers. Backed by the tough convicts in the camp, Shi En opened businesses there and collected a monthly share of commercial earnings, enjoying a comfortable life. Then Jiang the Door God appeared. His surname was Jiang and his given name Zhong; standing nine feet tall, he made his living as a wrestler and boasted that no opponent had beaten him at Mount Tai in three years. Supported by Zhang Mengfang, the military superintendent of Mengzhou's defense forces, he gave Shi En a savage beating and seized Happy Grove. Shi En suffered broken ribs as well as the loss of his business. He hated Jiang but could do nothing against him, so he swallowed his anger and looked for a hero powerful enough to avenge him.

At that very time, Wu Song the Pilgrim arrived at the camp run by Shi En's father, having been sentenced to exile in Mengzhou for killing Ximen Qing. New prisoners normally received a hundred intimidating blows, but Shi En secretly arranged for Wu Song to be spared. He lodged him in a clean room and treated him attentively to fine wine and meat every day. Wu Song was puzzled and questioned him repeatedly until Shi En explained how Happy Grove had been stolen and asked for revenge. Wu Song readily agreed on one condition: he wanted thirty-five bowls of wine, declaring that he would pass no wine-shop sign without drinking three bowls. Thus began the celebrated episode of the drunken beating of Jiang the Door God. Wu Song drank heavily along the road, reached Happy Grove and deliberately made trouble to draw Jiang out. With a few punches and kicks, including his Jade Ring Steps and Mandarin Duck Kicks, he knocked the boastful wrestling instructor flat. He forced Jiang to surrender, beg for mercy and leave Mengzhou that very night, restoring Happy Grove to Shi En. Grateful for this kindness, Shi En became Wu Song's friend in life and death.

Their good fortune did not last. Jiang refused to accept defeat and persuaded Military Superintendent Zhang and Training Officer Zhang to set a trap. They pretended to favor Wu Song by making him a personal attendant, then planted evidence of theft and confined him to death row. They also laid an ambush at Flying Cloud Ford to kill him. Wu Song killed the escorts at the ford, then drenched Mandarin Duck Tower in blood, slaying the two Zhang officials, Jiang and the rest of his enemies. Only then did he avenge the injustice and flee Mengzhou. Shi En was implicated because of their friendship. His family fortunes collapsed, and he abandoned Mengzhou to seek safety elsewhere. The two men then followed separate paths for a time. Wu Song joined Twin Dragon Mountain and later went to Liangshan after the three mountain bands united to attack Qingzhou. Around the same period, Shi En also sought refuge in the marsh and became a chieftain.

At Liangshan's grand assembly, the Heavenly and Earthly Stars received their places. Shi En corresponded to the Earthly Star of Ambush and occupied the eighty-fifth seat among the Earthly Stars, serving as an infantry officer available for assignment. He could fight with fists, feet, spear and staff and hold his own in battle. Yet his lasting fame rested chiefly on the name Golden-Eyed Leopard and the grudges and favors of Happy Grove; beside Liangshan's great warriors who led the charge, his military reputation was more modest.

After the amnesty, Shi En followed Song Jiang against the Liao and served in the campaigns against Tian Hu and Wang Qing, fighting north and south without shrinking from duty. Then came the southern war against Fang La, a bitter struggle in which more than half of Liangshan's chieftains were killed or wounded. Shi En crossed the river with the army and fought around Runzhou and Changzhou, where he fell into the water amid the confusion of battle and drowned, never returning home. From a local strongman at Happy Grove to Wu Song's companion in adversity, the Golden-Eyed Leopard ultimately died in imperial service for the cause he had joined. His story among the heroes of Water Margin is one of kindness repaid, loyalty sustained and a life carried through to its end.
施恩者，孟州人氏也，乃管营之子。其父在孟州牢城营做管营之职，掌管一营囚徒，施恩便.ja:
施恩は孟州の人で、牢城営の管営の息子である。父が一営の囚人を管理する地位にあったため、その権勢を頼みに孟州城の東、快活林で酒と肉を商う店を開き、往来の商人や賭場、妓楼からも上前を取って、一帯の顔役となっていた。幼いころから槍棒や拳脚を学び、ひととおりの武芸を身につけていた。黄みを帯びたつやのある顔、鋭い目つき、幾分か侠気のある振る舞いから、江湖では「金眼彪」と呼ばれた。「彪」は小虎のたぐいで、虎のような勇猛さを表し、「金眼」は両眼の鋭い輝きを形容する。その名のとおり、ただの道楽息子ではなく、胆力と腕力を備え、争いにもひるまぬ若者だった。

施恩の名が知られるようになったのは、快活林の一件による。孟州城の東にある快活林は東西の交通の要所で、商人や旅人が数多く行き交い、大小百軒ほどの店、賭場、両替屋が並んでいた。施恩は牢城営の腕自慢の囚人たちを後ろ盾に店を構え、毎月商いの上前を受け取り、気ままに暮らしていた。そこへ現れたのが蒋門神である。姓は蒋、名は忠、身の丈九尺の相撲取りで、泰山の相撲大会では三年間敵なしだったと豪語した。孟州守備の兵馬都監・張蒙方の勢力を頼み、施恩を打ちのめして快活林を奪った。施恩は肋骨を折られ、恨みを抱いたものの蒋門神には手が出せず、怒りをこらえて、自分に代わって仇を討てる豪傑を探していた。

折しも行者武松が西門慶を殺した罪で孟州へ流され、施恩の父が管轄する牢城営に入ってきた。新入りは慣例として百回の威しの棒打ちを受けるはずだったが、施恩はひそかに手を回して免除させた。さらに清潔な部屋をあてがい、毎日うまい酒と肉を出して手厚くもてなした。いぶかった武松が何度も問いただすと、施恩は快活林を奪われた顛末と、仇討ちを頼みたい胸の内を打ち明けた。武松は快諾し、ただ一つ、三十五杯の酒を飲ませてほしいと条件を出した。「酒旗を見れば三杯飲まずには通らぬ」というのである。これが名高い「酔って蒋門神を打つ」の一段となった。道々大いに酔った武松は快活林に着くと、まず騒ぎを起こして蒋門神を誘い出し、「玉環歩・鴛鴦脚」の妙技で傲慢な相撲師範を打ち倒した。降参して命乞いをさせ、その夜のうちに孟州から追い払い、快活林を施恩へ返した。施恩はこの恩義を深く感じ、武松と生死を共にする友となった。

しかし幸せは長く続かなかった。敗北を受け入れられない蒋門神は張都監と張団練を頼って罠を仕組んだ。武松を取り立てて近侍にするふりをしながら、盗みの濡れ衣を着せて死牢に入れ、さらに飛雲浦に伏兵を置いて命を奪おうとした。武松は飛雲浦で護送の役人を殺し、続いて鴛鴦楼へ乗り込み、張都監、張団練、蒋門神ら仇敵を斬った。大きな冤罪の恨みを晴らしたのち、孟州を逃れたのである。武松と親しかった施恩も巻き添えを受け、家業が傾き、孟州を捨てて他郷に難を避けるほかなかった。その後しばらく二人は別々の道を歩んだ。武松は二竜山へ入り、三山の豪傑が結集して青州を攻めたのち梁山へ移った。施恩もその前後に水泊へ身を寄せ、頭領の一人となった。

梁山の大集会で天罡・地煞の席次が定められると、施恩は地伏星にあたり、地煞の第八十五位に座した。歩兵の将校として命令に応じて働く役目である。拳脚、槍棒を使い、戦場で戦う力はあったが、その名を後世へ残したのは、何より「金眼彪」の異名と快活林の恩讐だった。突撃の先頭に立つ猛将たちと比べれば、軍功の名声は幾分控えめだった。

招安後は宋公明に従って遼を征し、田虎、王慶の討伐にも加わり、南北を転戦してひるむことなく軍務を果たした。やがて方臘への南征が始まり、この激戦で梁山頭領の半数以上が死傷した。施恩も軍と共に川を渡り、潤州、常州の一帯で戦ったが、乱戦のさなか水中へ落ちて溺死し、故郷へ帰ることはなかった。孟州快活林の顔役として出発した金眼彪施恩は、武松と知り合って患難を共にし、最後は大義に従って王事に殉じた。水滸の群雄の中でも、受けた恩を忘れず、義を貫いて生涯を終えた一人である。
施恩者，孟州人氏也，乃管营之子。其父在孟州牢城营做管营之职，掌管一营囚徒，施恩便.zh_TW:
施恩者，孟州人氏也，乃管營之子。其父在孟州牢城營做管營之職，掌管一營囚徒，施恩便倚著父親這點權勢，在孟州城東快活林一帶，開著一座酒肉店面，又嚮往來的客商、賭坊、妓館抽分使用，儼然是地面上的一霸。施恩自幼也曾使槍弄棒，學得一身好本事，使得幾路拳腳，江湖上的人見他麵皮生得黃潤，目光精悍，行事又有幾分豪俠氣概，便送他一個綽號，喚作「金眼彪」。這「彪」者，乃小虎之屬，言其勇悍如虎；「金眼」者，正狀其雙睛炯炯、精光四射之貌，合起來便見這少年管營之子，並非尋常紈絝，實是個有膽有力、能爭能斗的角色。

施恩之揚名，全在那快活林一段。原來孟州城東有一處去處，喚作快活林，乃東西往來的要道，過往商旅、閒人極多，那裡有百十處大小店面、賭坊、兌坊。施恩倚著營裡的好漢囚徒，在快活林開店設肆，每月坐收商稅分例，端的好不快活。不料半路里殺出一個蔣門神來。這蔣門神姓蔣名忠，身長九尺，相撲為業，自誇三年泰嶽爭交無對手，倚仗孟州守禦兵馬都監張蒙方之勢，把施恩痛打一頓，強奪了快活林去。施恩吃了這場虧，肋骨也被打折，心中懷恨，卻又奈何蔣門神不得，只得忍氣吞聲，欲尋一個了得的好漢與他報仇。

恰在此時，行者武松因鬥殺西門慶、刺配孟州牢城，正發在施恩父親所管的這座牢城營裡。武松初到，照例當吃一百殺威棒，施恩卻暗中囑託，不打他這頓棒；又每日好酒好肉相待，將武松安頓在一處淨房，殷勤奉承。武松起初不解，再三盤問，施恩方將快活林被奪、欲求報仇之事，一一告訴。武松聽罷，慨然應允，只提一個條件：要吃三十五碗酒，「無三不過望」，每過一處酒望子便吃三碗。這便是水滸中膾炙人口的「醉打蔣門神」。武松一路吃得爛醉，行到快活林，先尋鬧滋事，將蔣門神引出，三拳兩腳，使出「玉環步、鴛鴦腳」的絕技，把那誇口的相撲教頭打翻在地，逼他認輸求饒，連夜滾出孟州，將快活林依舊還了施恩。施恩自此感念武松恩義，結為生死之交。

誰知好景不長，蔣門神不甘心，去央張都監、張團練設下圈套，假意抬舉武松做了親隨，卻暗藏機關，誣陷武松偷盜，將他下在死牢，又于飛雲浦設伏，欲取性命。武松于飛雲浦殺了公人，又血濺鴛鴦樓，殺了張都監、張團練、蔣門神一干仇人，方才報了這場大冤，逃離孟州。施恩因與武松交厚，亦被牽連，家業敗落，只得棄了孟州，避禍他鄉。後來輾轉之間，二人各奔前程，武松歸了二龍山，三山聚義打青州，遂同上梁山。施恩亦在此前後投奔水泊，做了一員頭領。

梁山大聚義，排定天罡地煞座次，施恩上應地伏星，坐了第八十五把交椅，在地煞之列，職司步軍將校，聽候調遣。論施恩武藝，使得拳腳槍棒，臨陣亦能廝殺，然其名望，終究以「金眼彪」三字、快活林一段恩怨傳世，比之那些衝鋒陷陣的猛將，自是遜色幾分。

招安之後，施恩隨宋公明徵遼、平田虎王慶，皆在軍中效力，轉戰南北，未嘗退縮。及至南征方臘，這一場惡戰，梁山頭領死傷過半。施恩隨軍渡江，攻打潤州、常州一帶，於亂軍之中墮水而死，竟不曾生還故鄉。這「金眼彪」施恩，自孟州快活林一霸起，因結識武松、共歷患難，終隨大義歿於王事，亦是水滸群雄中一段有恩有義、有始有終的結局。

史进，绰号「九纹龙」，应天罡之数，乃天微星临世。其人乃华州华阴县史家村人氏，本是.en:
Shi Jin, nicknamed Nine-Tattooed Dragons, belonged to the Heavenly Stars as the earthly incarnation of the Heavenly Star of Subtlety. A native of Shi Family Village in Huayin County, Huazhou, he was the only beloved son of Elder Shi. As a boy he cared nothing for farming, preferring spear and staff practice. Unable to change his mind, his father hired seven or eight teachers, but Shi Jin found their instruction insufficient. Then Wang Jin, an instructor of the capital's eight hundred thousand imperial guards, arrived with his elderly mother while fleeing Gao Qiu's persecution. Elder Shi took them in to recover, and Shi Jin became Wang Jin's pupil. Over six months the master painstakingly taught him all eighteen martial disciplines from the beginning. Shi Jin absorbed the true art, becoming especially remarkable with a long staff. Nine green dragons were tattooed across his fine-skinned chest, shoulders and arms, giving him the name Nine-Tattooed Dragons throughout the county. Only eighteen or nineteen, with an imposing eight-foot frame and a handsome, spirited bearing, he was a striking young hero.

Shi Jin was the first hero to step onto the stage of Water Margin. After Wang Jin departed and Elder Shi died, he lived alone on the family estate. Three bandits then held Lesser Flower Mountain: Zhu Wu the Divine Strategist, Chen Da the Ravine-Leaping Tiger and Yang Chun the White-Spotted Snake. Against Zhu Wu's advice, Chen Da tried to pass through Shi Family Village to obtain grain in Huayin. Shi Jin rode out to oppose him and captured him alive. When Zhu Wu and Yang Chun heard the news, they did not attempt a rescue by force. Instead, they bound themselves and came to the estate, prepared to die beside Chen Da in the name of loyalty. Moved by their devotion, Shi Jin released his prisoner, befriended the three and secretly sent them money and gifts.

On the Mid-Autumn night, however, Shi Jin invited the three men to drink and admire the moon at his estate. A reply letter lost by his retainer Wang Si exposed their dealings, and Huayin sent troops to surround the manor. With no alternative, Shi Jin burned his own estate and fought his way out to Lesser Flower Mountain. Yet he did not wish to live as a bandit, so he left the others to search for Wang Jin in the west. Passing through Weizhou, he met Constable Lu Da, later the Flowery Monk Lu Zhishen, in a teahouse, and also encountered Li Zhong the Tiger-Slaying General. These meetings led to Lu Da's beating of the Bully of the West on behalf of Jin Cuilian and her father. Shi Jin and Lu Da became sworn brothers and later met again in Red Pine Forest.

Shi Jin's eventual journey to Liangshan took several turns. He returned to Lesser Flower Mountain and became its chief. Later he learned that Prefect He of Huazhou had seized Yu Jiaozhi, the daughter of the painter Wang Yi, and sent her father into penal exile. Outraged, Shi Jin entered Huazhou alone to assassinate the prefect and rid the people of a tyrant. His plan was discovered, however, and he was arrested and thrown into death row. Lu Zhishen heard of this and went alone to rescue him, only to be captured as well. Fortunately, Song Jiang brought the Liangshan army, tricked the defenders into opening the gates, took Huazhou and killed Prefect He. Shi Jin and Lu Zhishen were freed, after which Shi Jin, Zhu Wu, Chen Da, Yang Chun and their Lesser Flower Mountain followers all joined the great stronghold of Liangshan.

At Liangshan, Shi Jin could fight on horseback or on foot. He became one of the Eight Cavalry Vanguards, serving alongside Yang Zhi, Suo Chao, Xu Ning, Mu Hong and Hua Rong in the foremost ranks. At the grand assembly he received the twenty-third seat under the Heavenly Star of Subtlety. In the subsequent three assaults on Daming, two victories over Tong Guan and three defeats of Gao Qiu, he fought eagerly at the front and won repeated merit. Having learned Wang Jin's true teaching, he possessed a sound martial foundation and excelled particularly with the long staff and spear. He was indeed one of Liangshan's skilled and battle-tested young tiger generals.

After the amnesty, Shi Jin followed Song Jiang against the Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and finally against Fang La. That last campaign cost Liangshan more than half its brothers, and Shi Jin was among the dead. The army was attacking Yuling Pass near Muzhou, held by Fang La's general Pang Wanchun, the Little Yang Youji, whose archery was almost supernatural. Leading the vanguard, Shi Jin took Shi Xiu, Chen Da, Yang Chun, Li Zhong and Xue Yong ahead to scout. In a narrow stretch below the pass they fell into Pang Wanchun's ambush, and arrows flew from every side. Caught unprepared, all six men were struck and died below Yuling Pass. It was a bitter end for Nine-Tattooed Dragons: the fame of half a lifetime extinguished in a storm of arrows.

The first hero introduced in Water Margin, Shi Jin was a young man of chivalry who inherited a great master's teaching, valued loyalty and gave freely of his wealth. From burning his estate and becoming an outlaw to sacrificing his life at Yuling Pass, he remained an upright, open-hearted man willing to draw his blade against injustice. His name, Nine-Tattooed Dragons, resounded through the martial world. He opened the novel's long procession of heroes and ultimately died in imperial service, leaving among Liangshan's 108 champions a legend that began with dragons and ended in a generous act of loyalty.
史进，绰号「九纹龙」，应天罡之数，乃天微星临世。其人乃华州华阴县史家村人氏，本是.ja:
史進は「九紋竜」の異名を持ち、天罡の一員、天微星の化身にあたる。華州華陰県の史家村に生まれ、村の史太公が溺愛する一人息子だった。幼いころから農事には目もくれず、槍棒ばかりを好んだ。父もその性分を変えられず、七、八人の師匠を招いたが、史進は教えが浅いと不満を抱いていた。そこへ東京の八十万禁軍の教頭、王進が老母を連れて高俅の迫害を逃れ、史家村へやって来た。史太公が滞在させて養生を助けた縁で、史進は王進の弟子となった。王進は半年にわたり十八般の武芸を基礎から一つずつ授け、史進は奥義を受け継いだ。とりわけ長棒の技は神業の域に達した。美しい肌の胸、肩、腕には緑の九頭の竜が彫られており、そのため県中で九紋竜史進と呼ばれた。十八、九歳にして堂々たる八尺の体躯を持つ、凛々しく見栄えのする若武者だった。

史進は『水滸伝』で最初に本格的に登場する好漢である。王進が去り、史太公も亡くなると、史進は一人で屋敷を守った。当時、少華山には神機軍師の朱武、跳澗虎の陳達、白花蛇の楊春という三人の山賊が集まっていた。陳達は朱武の忠告を聞かず、華陰県へ糧食を取りに行くため史家村を通ろうとしたが、迎え撃った史進に生け捕られた。知らせを受けた朱武と楊春は力ずくで奪い返そうとはせず、自ら縄をかけて屋敷に赴き、義を全うするため陳達と共に死ぬことを願った。その深い義気に心を動かされた史進は陳達を放し、三人と交わりを結び、ひそかに金品を贈り合うようになった。

ところが中秋の夜、史進が三人を屋敷に招いて月見の酒宴を催すと、荘客の王四が返書を紛失したことから付き合いが露見し、華陰県の兵に屋敷を囲まれた。やむなく史進は自分の屋敷に火を放ち、包囲を突破して少華山へ逃れた。しかし山賊として暮らす気にはなれず、仲間に別れを告げ、関西へ師の王進を探しに出た。途中の渭州で茶店に立ち寄り、提轄の魯達、のちの花和尚魯智深と知り合い、打虎将の李忠とも出会った。ここから魯達が金翠蓮父娘のために鎮関西を殴り殺す一件が始まる。史進と魯達は義兄弟となり、のちに赤松林でも再会した。

史進が梁山に加わるまでには幾度もの曲折があった。やがて少華山へ戻って山賊となり、山寨の主に立った。その後、絵師王義の娘、玉嬌枝が華州の賀太守に奪われ、王義が流刑にされたことを知る。非道に憤った史進は民の害を除こうと、一人で華州へ潜入して賀太守の暗殺を企てた。しかし計画が漏れ、逆に捕らえられて死牢へ入れられた。魯智深も知らせを聞いて単身救出に向かったが、同じく捕まってしまった。幸い宋江が梁山の大軍を率いて来援し、計略で城門を開かせて華州を落とし、賀太守を殺して二人を救った。これを機に、史進と少華山の朱武、陳達、楊春らはそろって梁山の大寨へ加わった。

梁山に入った史進は騎戦にも歩戦にも優れ、楊志、索超、徐寧、穆弘、花栄らと並ぶ馬軍八驃騎兼先鋒使の一人となり、突撃を担った。大集会で席次が定まると、天微星として第二十三位に座した。その後の大名府への三度の攻撃、童貫に対する二度の勝利、高俅への三度の勝利にも勇んで先陣を切り、たびたび功を立てた。王進の正統な教えを受けて基礎が確かで、とくに長棒と槍法に長じた、梁山の若き歴戦の虎将だった。

招安後は宋江に従って遼、田虎、王慶を討ち、最後に方臘との戦いへ向かった。この戦役で梁山の兄弟は半数以上を失い、史進もまた命を落とした。軍が睦州の昱嶺関を攻めていたとき、関を守っていたのは方臘配下の小養由基こと龐万春で、神業のような弓術を誇った。先鋒の史進は石秀、陳達、楊春、李忠、薛永を率いる六人で偵察に出たが、関の下の狭い道で伏兵に遭い、一斉に矢を浴びた。不意を突かれた六人は全員が矢に倒れ、昱嶺関の下で戦死した。半生の名声を誇った九紋竜が、乱れ飛ぶ矢の中で散ったのである。

『水滸伝』の冒頭を飾る史進は、名師の真伝を受け、義を重んじ、財を惜しまず人に施す若い侠客だった。史家村の屋敷を焼いて山へ入った日から、昱嶺関で矢に倒れる日まで、常に公明正大で、不正を見れば刀を抜く気骨を失わなかった。「九紋竜」の名を江湖に響かせたこの若き英雄は、全編の幕を開け、やがて王事に殉じた。梁山泊の百八将の中に、竜を背負って現れ、義のために惜しみなく命を投じた独自の伝説を残している。
史进，绰号「九纹龙」，应天罡之数，乃天微星临世。其人乃华州华阴县史家村人氏，本是.zh_TW:
史進，綽號「九紋龍」，應天罡之數，乃天微星臨世。其人乃華州華陰縣史家村人氏，本是當村史太公的獨生愛子。自小不務農桑，只愛刺槍使棒，史太公拗他不過，請了七八個師父教導，史進卻嫌學得不精。後得遇東京八十萬禁軍教頭王進——王進因避高俅迫害，攜老母逃難至史家村，史太公留住調養，史進遂拜王進為師。王進盡心傳授，半年之間，將十八般武藝一一從頭指教，史進盡得真傳，更兼一條長棒，使得出神入化。史進生得一身好肌膚，胸膛肩臂共刺了九條龍，綠瑩瑩的，因此滿縣人都喚他做「九紋龍」史進。其年方十八九歲，凜凜一軀，堂堂八尺，少年英武，是個標緻後生。

史進之事，乃《水滸傳》全書第一個粉墨登場的好漢，王進辭別之後，史太公身故，史進獨守莊院。其時少華山上有三個強人:神機軍師朱武、跳澗虎陳達、白花蛇楊春，嘯聚山林。陳達不聽朱武之勸，要借路過史家村去華陰縣借糧，史進出莊迎戰，活捉了陳達。朱武、楊春聞知，並不來強奪，反自縛雙雙投到莊上，情願與陳達同死，以全義氣。史進感其義氣深重，遂釋了陳達，反與三人結納往來，私下饋贈財物。

不料中秋之夜，史進請三人入莊賞月飲酒，被莊客王四遺失回書，洩露行藏，華陰縣發兵圍莊。史進無奈，放火燒了自家莊院，殺出重圍，上了少華山。然史進不願落草為寇，辭別眾人，去關西尋師父王進，路經渭州，在茶坊結識提轄魯達（即後來的花和尚魯智深），又遇打虎將李忠，由此引出魯達拳打鎮關西、為金翠蓮父女出頭一段。史進與魯達自此結為兄弟，後又曾在赤松林重逢。

史進上梁山，幾經曲折。他後來回到少華山落草，做了山寨之主。後因畫匠王義之女玉嬌枝被華州賀太守強佔，王義被刺配，史進聞知不平，獨自潛入華州，要刺殺賀太守，為民除害。豈料事機不密，反被賀太守拿下，囚於死牢。魯智深聞訊，亦隻身去救，同樣被擒。幸得宋江率梁山大軍，賺開城門，攻破華州，殺了賀太守，救出史進、魯智深二人。自此史進並少華山朱武、陳達、楊春一行，盡數歸入梁山大寨。

既上梁山，史進馬上步下皆能征戰，是馬軍八驃騎兼先鋒使之一，與楊志、索超、徐寧、穆弘、花榮等同列，專司衝鋒。梁山大聚義，排定座次，史進應天微星，坐第二十三位。其後三打大名府、兩贏童貫、三敗高俅諸役，史進皆奮勇爭先，屢立戰功。論武藝，史進得王進真傳，根基極正，尤以長棒、槍法見長，端的是梁山一員能征慣戰的少年虎將。

招安之後，史進隨宋江徵遼，又徵田虎、王慶，再徵方臘。徵方臘之役，梁山兄弟損折大半，史進亦歿於此。其時大軍攻打睦州昱嶺關，關上守將乃方臘麾下小養由基龐萬春，善射，箭法如神。史進為先鋒，引石秀、陳達、楊春、李忠、薛永一行六人前去探路，行至關下狹隘處，中了龐萬春的埋伏，亂箭齊發。史進措手不及，與石秀等六人盡數中箭，死於昱嶺關下。可嘆一員九紋龍，半世英名，竟隕於亂箭之中。

史進一生，是《水滸傳》開卷第一好漢，得名師真傳，重義疏財，少年豪俠。自史家村放火落草，至昱嶺關中箭捐軀，始終是一條光明磊落、肯為不平拔刀的硬漢。這位以「九紋龍」三字名動江湖的少年英雄，開全書之端，亦終殞於王事，在梁山泊一百單八將之中，自有他這一段從龍起頭、慷慨赴義的傳奇。

时迁者，高唐州人氏，水浒一百单八将中第一等的神偷妙手。其人自小不务正业，专一飞檐.en:
Shi Qian, a native of Gaotangzhou, was the foremost master thief among the 108 heroes of Water Margin. From youth he had avoided honest work in favor of scaling roofs and walls, leaping fences, stealing horses, entering houses and slipping into camps to take whatever he wanted. His remarkable agility let him climb and leap without a sound, and no lock or binding seemed beyond his skill. He was a burglar of worldwide renown. Because he moved so lightly and quickly, bounding and climbing like a flea and making his way along eaves and roof beams, the martial world named him Flea on a Drum. The image evokes a flea springing across a taut drumhead without leaving a trace. Though scarcely a respectable title, it captured both his uncanny light-footed skill and his elusive nature as a thief. No one famous for stealth and climbing could surpass him.

Shi Qian's route to Liangshan was bound up with Yang Xiong, Sick Guan Suo, and Shi Xiu, Reckless Third. After Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu killed Pan Qiaoyun on Cuiping Mountain, they had nowhere to hide and set out for Liangshan. They met Shi Qian along the road and traveled together. While resting at an inn near Zhu Family Manor, Shi Qian gave in to his old habits. He noticed the inn's crowing rooster, could not resist it, and stole and killed the bird in the night to eat with his wine. The inn belonged to the Zhu estate. Its keeper discovered the theft and quarreled with the three travelers, who set the building alight. As they tried to leave, estate retainers captured Shi Qian and carried him into the manor. Unable to rescue him, Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu went to Liangshan for help, setting in motion the three assaults on Zhu Family Manor. A single stolen chicken provoked a bitter conflict between Liangshan and the Zhu estate. Song Jiang attacked three times, losing men and officers and suffering repeated setbacks before finally taking the manor and freeing Shi Qian. This notorious entrance into the story, in which chicken theft brought disaster and three campaigns, showed the trouble his craft could cause, but also brought him to Liangshan.

Once he had joined Liangshan, his thieving skills and agility became invaluable weapons. As Liangshan sought to draw Lu Junyi to the mountain, Xu Ning's hooked-lance technique was also essential to defeating the chained cavalry. Shi Qian was sent to the capital, entered Xu Ning's residence by night and crossed its roofs without being noticed. He stole Xu Ning's ancestral goose-feather golden armor, compelling its owner to come to the mountain and join the band. This theft of the armor to lure Xu Ning best displayed the height of Shi Qian's art. During the later attack on Zeng Family Town, he and Yu Baosi slipped inside, stole the signal-cannon tokens and acted as infiltrators, helping Liangshan destroy the settlement and avenge Chao Gai. No other commander could match him in stealing through camps, taking objects or gathering information in secret; his talent was unique. At the grand assembly, Shi Qian took the 107th seat as the Earthly Star of Theft. His army duties centered on carrying confidential messages, stealthy theft, climbing city walls and scouting enemy camps, making full use of the abilities that had earned him the name Flea on a Drum.

After the amnesty, Shi Qian accompanied the army on its northern and southern campaigns: against the great Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and finally Fang La. In the war against Fang La, his climbing and thieving skills remained highly effective. At crucial passes he was often the first over the walls, secretly preparing the way for his comrades and winning exceptional merit. Yet the dangerous rivers and mountains of the south took a terrible toll on Liangshan, whose heroes stained the southeast with their blood. Shi Qian did not fall to an enemy general's blade; he died of illness on the road. Once Fang La was subdued, the army returned toward the court. At Hangzhou, Shi Qian contracted an acute disease known as “twisting-gut sha,” suffered severe abdominal pain and died before he could return home. The Flea on a Drum had spent his life scaling roofs, stealing armor and infiltrating camps, earning extraordinary credit by luring Xu Ning and helping break Zeng Family Town. In the end, however, he could not escape a sudden illness and perished on the homeward march. The troublesome rooster at Zhu Family Manor, the stolen armor in Xu Ning's capital residence and the silent master thief passing over beams and eaves all faded with the scattering of Liangshan's stars. Only the name Flea on a Drum remained to recall his peerless mastery of the rooftops.
时迁者，高唐州人氏，水浒一百单八将中第一等的神偷妙手。其人自小不务正业，专一飞檐.ja:
時遷は高唐州の人で、水滸百八将の中でも随一の盗みの名手だった。幼いころから正業には就かず、屋根や壁を渡り、垣を越え、馬を盗み、人家や陣営へ忍び込むことを常としていた。身軽さは抜群で、高所へ登り、跳び移り、音もなく出入りし、錠前や縄を解くことにも自在の腕を持つ、天下に名高い盗賊だった。素早く軽やかに登り跳ね、蚤のように軒や梁を行き来するため、江湖では「鼓上蚤」と呼ばれた。張りつめた鼓の皮の上を蚤が自由に跳ね、跡も残さないという意味である。立派な呼び名とは言いがたいが、時遷の軽功の絶技と神出鬼没な盗人ぶりを生き生きと言い表していた。身軽さと盗みで名を立てた者の中に、彼をしのぐ者はいなかった。

時遷が梁山へ加わった経緯は、病関索の楊雄と拼命三郎の石秀に結びついている。楊雄と石秀は翠屏山で潘巧雲を殺し、身を隠す場所を失って梁山を目指した。その道中で時遷と出会い、三人で旅を続けた。祝家荘近くの宿で休んだとき、時遷は昔の悪癖を抑えられなかった。夜明けを告げる雄鶏を見つけると、夜中に盗んで殺し、酒の肴にしてしまったのである。宿は祝家荘に属しており、盗みに気づいた主人が三人と争いになった。時遷たちは宿に火をつけたが、立ち去ろうとして時遷が荘客に捕まり、荘内へ連行された。楊雄と石秀は救い出せず、梁山泊へ助けを求め、ここから三打祝家荘の大事件が始まった。たった一羽の鶏が梁山と祝家荘の激しい争いを招き、宋江は三度の攻撃で兵や将を失い、幾度も挫折した末にようやく荘を破って時遷を救った。鶏を盗んで災いを起こし、三度の征伐を引き起こしたこの一段は、時遷の登場場面として最も名高い。盗みが身を災いさせた一方、それが梁山へ至るきっかけともなった。

梁山へ入ると、時遷の盗みと軽功は大きな功を立てる武器になった。梁山が盧俊義を山へ誘おうとする一方、連環馬を破るには徐寧の鉤鎌槍法が欠かせなかった。命を受けた時遷は東京へ下り、真夜中に徐寧の屋敷へ潜入して屋根を渡り、誰にも気づかれずに家伝の雁翎金甲を盗み出した。これによって徐寧は山へ赴き、一味に加わることになった。「鎧を盗んで徐寧を誘う」の一件は、時遷の盗術の高さを最もよく示している。のちの曾頭市攻めでも、郁保四らと荘内へ忍び込み、合図の号砲に関わる印を盗んで内応し、梁山の勝利と晁蓋の仇討ちを助けた。陣営へ入り込んで物を盗み、ひそかに事情を探る仕事では、他の将に真似のできない異才だった。大集会では地賊星として第百七位に座し、軍中で機密の伝達、潜入盗取、城壁越え、陣営偵察といった重要な役目を担った。鼓上蚤の技が最も生きる分野である。

招安後、時遷は大軍と共に南北を転戦し、北の大遼、田虎、王慶を討ったのち、方臘への南征に加わった。方臘との戦いでも軽功と盗術を存分に発揮し、重要な関所では先に城壁を越えてひそかに味方を迎え入れるなど、数々の奇功を立てた。しかし江南の険しい山川は梁山の好漢に甚大な犠牲を強い、東南の地は血に染まった。時遷の最期は敵将の刃によるものではなく、道中の病死だった。方臘を平定して朝廷へ戻る途中、杭州で「絞腸痧」という急病にかかり、激しい腹痛の末に亡くなった。故郷へ生きて帰ることはかなわなかったのである。屋根や壁を自在に渡り、鎧を盗み、陣営を破った鼓上蚤は、その軽功と盗術で徐寧の誘致や曾頭市攻略に大きな功を立てたが、最後は急病を逃れられず、帰還の途上に倒れた。祝家荘で騒ぎを起こした雄鶏も、東京の徐家で盗まれた雁翎甲も、軒や梁を音なく渡った名人も、梁山の星々が散るのと共に塵へ帰った。後世に残る「鼓上蚤」の三文字が、天下無双の屋根渡りの技をしのばせている。
时迁者，高唐州人氏，水浒一百单八将中第一等的神偷妙手。其人自小不务正业，专一飞檐.zh_TW:
時遷者，高唐州人氏，水滸一百單八將中第一等的神偷妙手。其人自小不務正業，專一飛簷走壁、跳籬騙馬，慣做那穿房入戶、竊物偷營的勾當，一身輕功了得，攀高縱跳，來去無聲，開鎖解索，無所不能，乃是天下聞名的一個樑上君子。因他身手輕捷，行動迅疾，攀爬騰躍宛如跳蚤一般，又慣在屋簷房梁之上來去，江湖上的人便送他一個諢號，喚作「鼓上蚤」。鼓上蚤者，言其輕巧靈便，便如那能在繃緊的鼓面上蹦跳的跳蚤，縱躍自如而不留痕跡。以此為號，正狀時遷那一身輕功絕技、神出鬼沒的偷兒本色，聽來雖不甚體面，卻把他飛簷走壁的看家本領，狀得活靈活現，江湖中以輕功偷術著稱者，無人能出其右。

時遷上梁山的因由，系在病關索楊雄、拼命三郎石秀身上。當年楊雄、石秀在翠屏山殺了潘巧雲，無處藏身，欲投梁山，路上正遇著時遷，三人結伴同行。行至祝家莊左近的客店歇腳，時遷舊病復發，見店中有一隻報曉的公雞，便手癢難耐，半夜裡把那雞偷來殺了下酒。那店主人乃是祝家莊的店家，發覺雞被偷，與三人爭執起來，時遷等放火燒了店屋，要走時卻被祝家莊的莊客拿住，捉進莊裡去了。楊雄、石秀救他不得，只得往梁山泊求援，由此引出三打祝家莊這一場大事。為著時遷這一隻雞，惹動梁山與祝家莊的一場惡鬥，宋江三番攻打，損兵折將，幾番受挫，最終才大破祝家莊，把時遷救了出來。這一段偷雞惹禍、連累三打祝家莊，便是時遷登場最有名的一節，雖是為偷術所累，卻也由此把他引上了梁山。

時遷既上梁山，那一身偷術輕功，便成了梁山立功的一大利器。梁山要賺盧俊義上山，徐寧的鉤鐮槍法又是破連環馬的關鍵，時遷奉命下山，潛入東京徐寧府中，於半夜裡攀房越脊，神不知鬼不覺地盜了徐寧那祖傳的雁翎金甲，逼得徐寧不得不上山入夥，這「盜甲賺徐寧」一節，最見時遷偷術之高。後來攻打曾頭市，又是時遷與鬱保四等人，潛入莊中盜了號炮信物，做了內應，助梁山破了曾頭市，了結晁蓋的舊仇。凡此穿營盜物、潛行探事的勾當，梁山諸將無人能及，時遷實是獨一份的奇才。梁山大聚義，排定座次，時遷坐了第一百零七把交椅，上應地賊星，在軍中專一充當走報機密、潛行盜物、攀城探營的緊要差使，那一身鼓上蚤的本事，於這一道正是用得淋漓盡致。

招安以後，時遷隨大軍南征北討，北征大遼，復掃田虎、王慶，終而南下征討方臘。這一場平方臘之役，時遷那一身輕功偷術依舊大顯身手，攻打方臘的緊要關隘，往往是他先攀城越牆、暗中接應，立下不少奇功。怎奈江南山水險惡，梁山好漢死傷慘重，血染東南半壁。時遷的結局，卻不在敵將刀下，而是病死途中。大軍平定方臘，班師還朝，行至杭州，時遷途中染了「絞腸痧」這一種急症，腹中絞痛，竟一病而亡，歿於回軍路上，未能活著回到故鄉。一個飛簷走壁、盜甲破營的鼓上蚤，一生靠著那一身輕功偷術，為梁山立下賺徐寧、破曾頭市種種奇功，到頭來卻躲不過一場急病，零落在了班師的途中。祝家莊那隻惹禍的報曉雞，東京徐府那副被盜的雁翎甲，那個屋簷房梁之上來去無聲的神偷妙手，終究隨著梁山的星散而歸於塵土，徒留「鼓上蚤」三字，供後人追想他那一身天下無雙的飛簷絕技。

石秀，金陵建康府人氏，自幼父母双亡，流落江湖，曾随叔伯贩卖羊马，往来各处做些买卖.en:
Shi Xiu came from Jiankang Prefecture in Jinling. Orphaned as a child, he wandered the martial world and once traded sheep and horses with an uncle, traveling from place to place on business. When their capital was lost and his uncle died far from home, Shi Xiu drifted to Jizhou and survived by carrying and selling firewood. He was sharp-eyed and quick-handed, both daring and meticulous. Above all, he could never pass an injustice without drawing his blade to help; once he saw wrongdoing, he was prepared to risk his life to intervene. This won him the nickname Reckless Third, a name expressing his readiness to fight without regard for life or death whenever someone was wronged.

Strongly built and skilled with a long-handled broadsword, Shi Xiu combined accomplished martial arts with unusual alertness. He read expressions and situations with great clarity, making him one of the more observant heroes of Water Margin. On a street in Jizhou, he encountered Yang Xiong returning from an execution and being harassed and humiliated by a gang of hooligans. Shi Xiu stepped forward, scattered them with a few blows and rescued him. Admiring both his loyalty and his skill, Yang Xiong became his sworn brother and took him home. He then recommended Shi Xiu to his father-in-law, Elder Pan, who reopened a meat shop with Shi Xiu's help.

Though working as a butcher, Shi Xiu remained keenly observant. He noticed suspicious behavior in Yang Xiong's wife, Pan Qiaoyun, and frequent visits by Pei Ruhai, a monk of Bao'en Temple. Watching carefully, he uncovered their affair and even learned the secret signal used by the ascetic Hu Dao, who struck a wooden fish at dawn to keep watch for the adulterous monk. Shi Xiu told Yang Xiong, but Pan Qiaoyun accused him first, falsely claiming that he had harassed her. Believing his wife, Yang Xiong distanced himself from Shi Xiu and closed the meat shop. Shi Xiu did not argue with his sworn brother over the injustice. Instead, he resolved to prove the affair and clear Yang Xiong's shame. Waiting at night in the lane used by the monk, he first killed Hu Dao, then Pei Ruhai. He stripped off their clothing and left their bodies in the street so that the whole city would learn of the affair. This episode of investigation and killing revealed both the depth of his planning and the ruthlessness of his methods.

Afterward, Shi Xiu found Yang Xiong and explained the truth, restoring their friendship. Together they went to Cuiping Mountain, lured Pan Qiaoyun and her maid Ying'er there, and Yang Xiong killed his wife in revenge. With nowhere to hide after the killings, they set out for Liangshan and met the master thief Shi Qian, who joined them. Near Zhu Family Manor, Shi Qian stole a chicken, caused a quarrel and was captured by the estate's retainers. Shi Xiu and Yang Xiong sought help at Liangshan, leading to the three assaults on the manor. The first two attacks failed because of its deceptive, twisting roads and difficult terrain. Shi Xiu volunteered for the dangerous task of entering alone, disguised as a woodcutter. Inside he befriended an elderly man named Zhong Li and learned the secret of the maze: turn at the winding paths, and look for white poplars to find a way through. He also rescued the chieftains trapped within. During the third assault, he coordinated with the army from inside, guided Liangshan's forces through the maze and helped take Zhu Family Manor, earning foremost credit. The episode demonstrated that his courage was matched by intelligence and resourcefulness.

At Liangshan's grand assembly, Shi Xiu took the thirty-third seat among the Heavenly Stars as the Heavenly Star of Wisdom. He served with Yang Xiong as an infantry chieftain and often undertook reconnaissance, infiltration and assaults on difficult positions. His careful mind and courage made him especially suited to secret and dangerous work. Later, after Lu Junyi had been drawn into Liangshan's affairs and then framed, he was imprisoned in Daming and led to the execution ground. Shi Xiu entered the Northern Capital alone. At the execution site, he leaped from an upper floor of a tavern, shouted and swung his blade to interrupt the sentence, attempting single-handedly to save Lu Junyi and cutting a bloody path through the crowd. Though outnumbered and captured, he showed no fear and cursed Grand Secretary Liang. This attempt to storm the execution ground displayed the true character of Reckless Third, and above all his loyal heart and fearless devotion to a friend.

After the amnesty, Shi Xiu followed the army against the Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, campaigning without rest. During the war against Fang La, he joined Shi Jin and four other generals in the attack on Yuling Pass. The six fell into an ambush laid by Pang Wanchun, the Little Yang Youji. Arrows rained upon them, and Shi Xiu died with Shi Jin and the others below the pass. Throughout his life, Reckless Third had risked himself for loyalty: exposing an affair for a friend, breaking into an execution ground to save a man, scouting an estate and piercing its defenses. Even at the end he was in the foremost ranks, dying under a volley of arrows. He fulfilled the “reckless” promise of his name, spilling his ardent blood among the mountain passes of the south and leaving a story that invites a long, sorrowful sigh.
石秀，金陵建康府人氏，自幼父母双亡，流落江湖，曾随叔伯贩卖羊马，往来各处做些买卖.ja:
石秀は金陵の建康府の出身で、幼くして父母を失い、江湖を流浪した。かつて叔父と羊や馬を売り、各地を往来して商いをしていたが、元手を失い、叔父も旅先で亡くなると、薊州へ流れ着き、薪を担いで売る暮らしとなった。目も手も素早く、大胆でありながら細心だった。何より不正を見過ごせず、道で困っている者を見れば刀を抜いて助け、命を懸けても口を出す性分だった。そこから江湖では「拼命三郎」と呼ばれた。生死を顧みず、戦うべきときには戦い、不義には命を賭して立ち向かう男という意味である。

石秀は丈夫な体つきで、朴刀を巧みに使い、武芸に熟達していた。それに加えて機転が利き、人の言葉や顔色から事情を見抜く、群雄の中でも珍しく注意深い人物だった。薊州の街で、処刑を終えて戻る楊雄が無頼漢たちに絡まれ、辱められている場面に出くわすと、進み出て数発の拳脚で一味を追い散らし、楊雄を救った。楊雄はその義気と武芸を敬い、義兄弟の契りを結んで家へ招いた。さらに舅の潘公に勧め、石秀の助けで肉屋を再開して、屠畜の商いを始めさせた。

肉屋として働いていても、石秀の目は鋭かった。楊雄の妻、潘巧雲の振る舞いに不審を感じ、報恩寺の僧、裴如海が頻繁に出入りすることに気づいて、ひそかに様子を探った。やがて二人の密通を突き止め、頭陀の胡道が毎夜、木魚を打って夜明けを知らせ、僧のために見張りをする合図までつかんだ。楊雄に告げたものの、潘巧雲は先手を打ち、石秀に言い寄られたと逆に訴えた。妻を信じた楊雄は石秀を遠ざけ、肉屋も閉めた。濡れ衣を着せられた石秀は兄と争わず、密通を確かな証拠で示し、楊雄の恥を晴らそうと決めた。深夜、僧の通る路地で待ち、まず夜明けを告げる胡道を殺し、次に裴如海を斬った。衣服を剥ぎ、死体を街路へさらして、密通を町中に知らしめたのである。この調査と殺僧の一段には、石秀の深い計略と容赦のない手段がよく表れている。

その後、石秀は楊雄を探して真相を説明し、二人は元どおりに和解した。共に翠屏山へ行き、潘巧雲と侍女の迎児を誘い出し、楊雄が妻を斬って恨みを晴らした。殺人ののち身を隠す場所を失った二人は梁山へ向かい、途中で盗みの名人、時遷と出会って三人で旅を続けた。祝家荘に至ると、時遷が鶏を盗んで騒ぎを起こし、荘客に捕まった。石秀と楊雄が梁山へ救援を求めたことで、三打祝家荘が始まった。最初の二度の攻撃は、複雑な地形と人を惑わす盤陀路に阻まれた。石秀は危険な役目を買って出て、一人で木こりに扮し、荘の奥へ入って地理を探った。老人の鍾離と知り合い、「盤陀に出会えば曲がり、白楊が見えれば通れる道」という迷路の仕組みを聞き出し、荘内に取り残された頭領たちも救った。三度目の攻撃では内外から呼応し、梁山軍を盤陀路の先へ導いて荘を破り、大きな功を立てた。勇気だけでなく知恵と度胸も兼ね備えていることを示す場面である。

梁山の大集会で、石秀は天罡の天慧星として第三十三位に座した。楊雄と共に歩兵頭領を務めるほか、偵察、潜入、難所への攻撃を任されることも多かった。綿密な思考と胆力を備え、機密を扱う危険な任務に最も適していたためである。のちに盧俊義が梁山の計略に巻き込まれ、さらに陥れられて大名府の牢へ入り、処刑場へ引かれることになった。石秀は一人で北京大名府へ潜入し、処刑場に面した酒楼から飛び降り、大喝して刀を振るい、単身で盧俊義を救おうと血路を開いた。多勢に無勢で捕らえられ、牢に入れられても少しも恐れず、梁中書を罵った。まさに拼命三郎の本領であり、この処刑場での救出劇は、その忠義と胆力を際立たせている。

招安後、石秀は大軍に従って遼、田虎、王慶と休むことなく戦った。方臘討伐で昱嶺関を攻めた際、史進、石秀ら六将は小養由基こと龐万春の伏兵にかかり、一斉に矢を浴びた。石秀も史進らと共に矢に倒れ、関の下で戦死した。友のために密通を暴き、人を救うために処刑場へ躍り込み、荘内を探って陣を破るなど、この拼命三郎は生涯を通じて義のために命を懸けた。最期まで先頭に立ち、乱れ飛ぶ矢の中で倒れた姿は、まさに「拼命」の二文字にふさわしい。その熱い血が江南の山関に流れたことを思えば、深いため息を禁じ得ない。
石秀，金陵建康府人氏，自幼父母双亡，流落江湖，曾随叔伯贩卖羊马，往来各处做些买卖.zh_TW:
石秀，金陵建康府人氏，自幼父母雙亡，流落江湖，曾隨叔伯販賣羊馬，往來各處做些買賣。後因本錢折盡，叔伯又客死他鄉，石秀淪落到薊州，以挑柴賣薪度日，落魄街頭。其人生得眼明手快，膽大心細，平生最是路見不平、拔刀相助，一身好膽，遇著不平之事，便要拼著性命去管，因此江湖上送他一個綽號，喚作「拼命三郎」。蓋言其行事不顧死生、敢拼敢搏，凡有不平，必以命相爭。

石秀身材健壯，使一口好朴刀，武藝精熟，更兼為人機警，察言觀色，洞若觀火，乃是水滸群雄中難得的細心人。他在薊州街頭，正撞見楊雄行刑回來，被一夥潑皮無賴糾纏羞辱，石秀挺身而出，三拳兩腳打散了那夥人，救了楊雄。楊雄見他義氣，又敬他武藝，遂與他結為兄弟，引回家中，又薦他幫丈人潘公重開肉鋪，做起屠宰生意。

石秀雖做屠戶營生，卻心思細密。他察覺楊雄之妻潘巧雲行止有異，又見報恩寺和尚裴如海時常出入，便留心窺探，終於訪得潘巧雲與裴如海私通的實情，連那頭陀胡道每夜敲木魚報曉、為奸僧把更的暗號也一一拿準。石秀將此事告與楊雄，不料潘巧雲惡人先告狀，反誣石秀調戲於她，楊雄聽信婦言，疏遠石秀，收了肉鋪。石秀蒙此不白之冤，卻不與兄長爭辯，隻立意要將姦情坐實，替楊雄雪恥。他於深夜守在僧人來往的巷口，先一刀結果了報曉的頭陀胡道，又殺了奸僧裴如海，剝下衣物，將屍首陳於街心，使滿城皆知姦情。此一段訪奸、殺僧，最見石秀心機之深、手段之辣。

事後石秀尋見楊雄，剖明真相，二人和好如初，又同上翠屏山，賺出潘巧雲與丫鬟迎兒，楊雄手刃妻仇。殺人之後，二人無處藏身，正欲投奔梁山，路遇神偷時遷，三人結伴同行。行至祝家莊，時遷偷雞惹禍，被莊客拿去。石秀、楊雄往梁山求援，引出三打祝家莊。頭打、二打皆因祝家莊盤陀路詐、地形複雜而受挫，石秀臨危請纓，獨自一人扮作樵夫，深入祝家莊打探地理，結識了莊中老人鍾離，問明那「遇盤陀便轉彎，見白楊樹便是活路」的盤陀路機關，又救出陷在莊中的眾頭領。三打之際，石秀裡應外合，引梁山軍馬破了盤陀路，大破祝家莊，立下首功。這一節正顯出石秀有勇有謀、智深膽壯的過人之處。

梁山大聚義，石秀位列天罡，應天慧星，排第三十三位，與楊雄同掌步軍頭領，又常擔當哨探、潛行、攻堅之任，蓋因他心思縝密、膽識俱全，最宜行此機密危險之事。後來盧俊義陷於大名府，被梁山賺來又遭陷害，將赴法場處斬，石秀隻身潛入北京大名府，於法場之上，從酒樓飛身躍下，一聲大喝，揮刀劫法場，獨力救盧俊義，殺開一條血路，雖寡不敵眾被擒入獄，卻面無懼色，痛罵梁中書，端的是拼命三郎的本色，此一節劫法場救盧俊義，尤見其義膽忠肝。

招安之後，石秀隨大軍徵遼，又徵田虎、王慶，轉戰不息。及至征討方臘，攻打昱嶺關時，史進、石秀等六將中了龐萬春小養由基的埋伏，亂箭齊發，石秀與史進等同時中箭身亡，歿於關下。這位拼命三郎，一生為義拼命，訪奸為友、劫法救人、探莊破陣，臨到末路，仍是衝鋒在前，死於亂箭，正應了那「拼命」二字，一腔熱血，灑於江南山關之間，令人扼腕長嘆。

石将军石勇，大名府人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地丑星的好汉，坐第九十九把交椅。这.en:
Shi Yong, Stone General, came from Daming Prefecture. Among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes, he embodied the Earthly Star of Ugliness and held the 99th seat. Tall, rough-featured and immensely strong, he had been an idle fellow devoted to gambling and throwing his weight about. Dice were his greatest pleasure, and his overbearing temper feared neither heaven nor earth. During a quarrel at a Daming gambling house, he killed a man with his fists and feet. Facing a murder charge, he fled his home and became a fugitive. Friends in the martial world saw his fierce looks, stubborn nature and readiness to strike or kill, and teasingly named him Stone General. He had never actually been a general: the name mocked his swaggering ferocity, which made him look like a killer marching into battle.

After fleeing Daming, Shi Yong found refuge on the estate of Chai Jin, Little Whirlwind, in Henghai Commandery, Cangzhou. Chai Jin was generous and righteous, welcoming unfortunate heroes from everywhere, and Shi Yong stayed with him for a time. Later he left to seek another place to settle, reaching Shandong and beginning the chain of events that joined him to Liangshan. His path to the mountain differed from that of others. He did not first become an outlaw and then join the band; instead, he met its heroes through delivering a crucial letter to Song Jiang. Song Jiang had killed Yan Poxi and was wandering as a fugitive. Shi Yong happened to encounter him at an inn in Jieyang Town, shortly after Song Jiang arrived there. Carrying a letter from the Song household, he had been searching everywhere for Song Gongming at Old Master Song's request. They nearly came to blows over a seat. Only after exchanging names did Shi Yong realize that the man before him was the filial and righteous Dark Third Brother whom he sought. He hastily bowed down and presented the letter. Song Jiang opened it to find a false report that his father had died and an urgent summons to return for the funeral. This deceptive letter, designed to draw him home, reached his hands through Shi Yong. Song Jiang returned, fell into danger again and passed through further reversals; Shi Yong eventually followed the same chain of connections to Liangshan.

After Shi Yong joined the mountain, his experience as a gambling fugitive and a seasoned wanderer made him useful in receiving visitors, guarding passes and gathering intelligence. He was an alert, dependable man for errands and practical duties. At Liangshan's great assembly and ranking of the heroes, he joined the earthly stars as the Earthly Star of Ugliness, occupying the 99th seat. Appointed an infantry officer, he often marched and fought with the main army. He served alongside the others in the fierce battles that twice defeated Tong Guan and three times overcame Gao Qiu, never shirking his part.

After the amnesty, Shi Yong followed Song Jiang's army north and south, fighting the Liao, suppressing Tian Hu and Wang Qing, and campaigning against Fang La in Jiangnan. He devoted himself throughout these wars, until the assault on Shezhou cost him his life. Inside the city was Fang La's Minister of War, Wang Yin, nicknamed Rival to Zhang Fei, an exceptionally skilled warrior armed with a spear and mounted on a swift horse. As Liangshan's troops entered the city, they met Wang Yin forcing a path out. Li Yun, Blue-Eyed Tiger, first advanced on foot with his saber, but Wang Yin charged and trampled him to death. Seeing his companion fall, Shi Yong hurried forward to fight Wang Yin and avenge him. Their skills were far apart, however, and a foot soldier faced a mounted man at a grave disadvantage. Within a few exchanges, Wang Yin killed Shi Yong with a thrust of his spear. He and Li Yun died one after the other before the same formidable enemy's horse. Alas for Stone General: he had fled a deadly gambling quarrel in Daming, spent half his life on the run, carried Song Jiang's letter and followed Liangshan across the land. His story ended with neither peaceful spiritual release nor an official appointment. Beneath Shezhou's walls, he and Li Yun became two wronged souls amid the blades and spears. As though answering the name Earthly Star of Ugliness, he disappeared quietly into the chaos of battle, another Water Margin hero denied a peaceful end.
石将军石勇，大名府人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地丑星的好汉，坐第九十九把交椅。这.ja:
石将軍・石勇は大名府の出身で、梁山泊百八人の好漢のうち地醜星に応じ、第九十九位に座した。背が高く、顔つきは粗野で、腕力は並外れていたが、もとは定職も持たず、賭博と喧嘩に明け暮れる男であった。とりわけ賽を振るのが好きで、天も地も恐れぬ横暴な気性を持っていた。大名府の賭場で勝負をめぐって腹を立て、人を殴り蹴りして殺してしまい、殺人の罪を逃れるため故郷を捨て、江湖をさすらう身となった。江湖の仲間は、凶悪な顔と強情な性格、何かと殴る殺すと言い出す様子を見て、からかい半分に「石将軍」と呼んだ。実際に将軍だったわけではなく、その荒々しい勇みぶりが、戦場へ出る殺し屋そっくりだと笑ったのである。

大名府を逃れた石勇は、滄州横海郡にある小旋風・柴進の屋敷を頼った。柴進は義を重んじて財を惜しまず、天下の窮した好漢を広く迎えていたので、石勇もしばらくその世話になった。やがて屋敷を離れ、新たな身の置き所を求めて山東へ入り、梁山との縁を結ぶことになる。ただし、その入山のいきさつは他の者と違っていた。先に山賊となって仲間入りしたのではなく、宋江に大切な家書を届けたことが、梁山の人々との出会いにつながったのである。当時、宋江は閻婆惜を殺して逃亡し、江湖を流浪していた。石勇は掲陽鎮の酒屋で、そこへ着いたばかりの宋江に偶然出会った。宋家の手紙を懐にし、宋太公の命を受けて宋公明の行方を探し回っていたのである。二人は席を取り合って口論となり、つかみ合いになりかけたが、名を明かして初めて、石勇は目の前の男が探していた孝義黒三郎だと知った。慌ててひざまずき、家書を差し出した。宋江が封を切ると、父の宋太公が亡くなったので急ぎ帰郷して葬儀に参じよ、と偽りが記されていた。宋江を故郷へ誘い戻すこの手紙を、まさに石勇が届けたのである。その後、宋江は帰郷して再び難に遭い、幾度もの曲折を経た。石勇もまた、この一連の縁をたどって梁山へ加わった。

入山後の石勇は、賭博者であり逃亡者として江湖を渡り歩いた経験を買われ、客の出迎えや見送り、関所の守備、情報収集などを任されることが多かった。使い走りや雑務に機転を利かせる、頼りになる人物であった。梁山の大集会で席次が定まると、地煞に列し、地醜星として第九十九位を占めた。歩軍の将校となって大軍に従い、しばしば出征して戦った。童貫を二度破り、高俅を三度退けた激戦にも皆とともに力を尽くし、身を引くことはなかった。

招安後は宋江の大軍に従い、遼の征討、田虎と王慶の平定、江南の方臘討伐と、南北に転戦して命を尽くした。そして方臘方の歙州を攻めた一戦で、ついに命を落とした。歙州城には方臘配下の兵部尚書・王寅がいた。「賽張飛」と呼ばれるこの男は、槍を巧みに使い、駿馬を駆る、きわめて武芸の優れた武将であった。梁山軍が城内へ殺到したとき、道を開いて脱出しようとする王寅と出くわした。まず青眼虎・李雲が刀を手に徒歩で挑んだが、王寅に馬を躍らせて突っ込まれ、その場で踏み殺された。仲間の死を見た石勇は仇を討とうと身を挺して進み出た。しかし武芸の差は大きく、しかも徒歩と騎馬では勢いが釣り合わない。数合も交えぬうちに王寅の槍で討ち取られ、李雲と前後して、同じ方臘方の猛将の馬前に果てた。哀れな石将軍・石勇よ。大名府の命を懸けた賭場の殺人から逃れ、半生を流浪し、宋江へ書を届けて縁をつなぎ、梁山とともに南北を戦った末に、安らかな坐化も官位も得ることはなかった。ただ歙州の城下で李雲とともに刀槍の中の冤魂となり、「地醜星」の名に応じるかのように乱軍の中へひそかに消えた。水滸の群雄の中でも、穏やかな最期を得られなかった一人である。
石将军石勇，大名府人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地丑星的好汉，坐第九十九把交椅。这.zh_TW:
石將軍石勇，大名府人氏，乃梁山泊一百單八將中應地醜星的好漢，坐第九十九把交椅。這石勇生得身材高大、面貌粗豪，膂力過人，本是個遊手好閒、專一賭錢使氣的漢子。他平日裡最好的便是擲骰賭博，又生就一副天不怕地不怕的橫強脾氣，在大名府賭場上，因爭賭使性，一拳一腳把人打死了，吃了人命官司，不得已逃出鄉里、亡命江湖。江湖上的朋友見他生得兇惡、性子剛強、動輒要打要殺，便戲送他一個諢名，喚作「石將軍」——並非他真做過甚麼將軍，乃是取笑他那一身橫勇煞氣、活像個上陣的殺才罷了。

石勇打死人逃出大名府後，一路投奔到滄州橫海郡的小旋風柴進莊上安身。柴進仗義疏財、專一招攬天下落難好漢，石勇便在柴大官人莊上盤桓了些時日。後來他離了柴進莊，要去尋一處去處，行至山東地面，方與梁山結下緣法。說來這石勇上山的因由，倒與旁人不同——他不是先落草、後入夥，乃是因替宋江傳遞了一封要緊家書，才與梁山眾人會合的。其時宋江殺了閻婆惜，正逃難在外、流落江湖。石勇在揭陽鎮一處酒店裡，與初到此地的宋江偶然相逢；他原是揣著一封宋家的書信，奉宋太公之命，四處尋訪宋公明下落的。兩人在酒店裡幾乎因爭座位口角廝打，待通了姓名，石勇方知面前正是自己要尋的孝義黑三郎，慌忙拜倒，呈上家書。宋江拆書一看，書中詐稱父親宋太公已經亡故、急召他回家奔喪——這一封賺他回鄉的家書，正是出自石勇之手遞到。後來宋江回鄉、再度落難，幾經輾轉，石勇也隨這一脈機緣歸了梁山。

石勇上山之後，因他原是賭徒亡命、慣走江湖，山寨裡多教他料理迎來送往、把守關隘、探聽訊息一類的勾當，是個跑腿應差、機警可用的腳色。梁山大聚義、英雄排座次時，石勇位列地煞，上應地醜星，坐第九十九位，充作步軍將校，常隨大隊出征廝殺。兩贏童貫、三敗高俅諸番惡戰，他亦隨眾效力，不曾退避。

受了招安之後，石勇隨宋江大軍南征北討，徵遼、平田虎王慶、下江南打方臘，一路捐軀效命。及至大軍攻打方臘的歙州，便在這一陣上殞了性命。原來歙州城中有方臘麾下兵部尚書王寅，綽號「賽張飛」，使一條好槍、騎一匹快馬，武藝極是高強。梁山軍馬殺入城內之時，正撞著王寅奪路突圍：先是青眼虎李雲提刀上前步戰，被王寅縱馬一衝、當場踏死；石勇見同伴折了，挺身趕上前去，要與王寅交手報仇。怎奈兩人武藝相去甚遠，又是一步一騎、勢不相敵，不上幾個回合，石勇便被王寅一槍結果了性命，與李雲一前一後，同死於這一員方臘勇將的馬前。可嘆這石將軍石勇，自大名府一樁賭命的人命案逃出，半生亡命、為宋江傳書牽線、又隨梁山轉戰南北，到頭來既不曾坐化、亦不曾封官，只在歙州城下與李雲同做了刀槍叢裡的兩個冤魂，應著那「地醜星」的星名，悄然歿於亂軍，是水滸眾豪裡又一個不得善終的好漢。

宋江，字公明，郓城县宋家村人氏。其面黑身矮，人皆唤作「黑宋江」；又因平生仗义疏财.en:
Song Jiang, courtesy name Gongming, came from Song Family Village in Yuncheng County. His dark face and short stature earned him the name Dark Song Jiang. All his life he upheld righteousness, gave money freely, relieved poverty and helped those in distress. His reputation spread throughout the martial world, and all who heard his name in Shandong and Hebei respected him, calling him Timely Rain. For his devotion to his parents, his neighbors called him the filial and righteous Dark Third Brother. His other name, Protector of Righteousness, expressed his own claim to be a righteous man who protected the country and brought peace to its people, and thus declared his loyal intentions.

Song Jiang first served as a clerk in Yuncheng County. He was adept with legal documents and well versed in official practice; he also loved spear and staff exercises and learned several martial arts. Gentle in manner but firm within, he enjoyed befriending heroes from every quarter. Whoever came to him, high or low, received hospitality on his estate, and when they wished to leave he supplied their expenses. He truly spent gold as though it were dust. Heroes throughout the land felt such gratitude for his generosity and loyalty that they were willing to die for him.

Song Jiang's road to Liangshan began when he secretly allowed Chao Gai to escape. After the birthday tribute robbery by Chao Gai and his six companions was exposed, officials sent men to arrest them. Song Jiang learned of it and warned Chao Gai overnight, allowing him to flee to Liangshan. Later, his mistress Yan Poxi used a letter from Liangshan to threaten him. Enraged, Song Jiang killed her, faced prosecution and was sentenced to tattooing and exile in Jiangzhou. Passing Liangshan, Jieyang Ridge and other places, he met many heroes. In Jiangzhou he became close to Dai Zong and Li Kui. One drunken day he wrote a rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower. Huang Wenbing reported him, and he was condemned to death. At the moment of execution, Chao Gai led Liangshan's heroes in a raid on the execution ground and rescued him, while Li Kui fought with his broad axes in a killing frenzy. Only then did Song Jiang become an outlaw and go up to Liangshan.

After Chao Gai was fatally wounded by an arrow, his last command promised leadership to whoever captured Shi Wengong. Lu Junyi later made the capture, but the assembled heroes supported Song Jiang, who ultimately took the first seat as Liangshan Marsh's supreme leader. He occupied the Heavenly Star of Leadership, foremost among the 108. On the mountain he established banners, assigned duties, founded the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and raised the apricot-yellow banner proclaiming, "Carry Out Heaven's Will." Loyalty and righteousness were his call to the heroes. Though his martial skill fell short of Lin Chong, Guan Sheng and the other great warriors, his kindness, trustworthiness and moral standing won their allegiance. He deployed forces capably and planned within his command tent, uniting the Thirty-Six Heavenly Stars and Seventy-Two Earthly Stars in common effort under his orders. He directed the three attacks on Zhu Family Manor, the defeat of the chained cavalry, the assault on Zeng Family Town, the two victories over Tong Guan and the three defeats of Gao Qiu.

Song Jiang's lifelong ambition lay in amnesty, not outlaw life. Remembering both the grievances and obligations bound up with his sentence of tattooing and exile, and cherishing loyalty to the ruler and country, he continually hoped that the emperor would soon issue an amnesty decree. Through Grand Marshal Su and Yan Qing, Emperor Huizong was at last persuaded to change his mind. The court proclaimed the amnesty, and all Liangshan's heroes submitted. Song Jiang then led the army against the Great Liao, crushing its forces and winning distinction. Next he was ordered to suppress Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi, returning victorious from both campaigns. Finally came the imperial command to march south against Fang La. This was the most terrible campaign: Jiangnan's mountains and rivers were treacherous, Fang La's army immense, and Liangshan lost more than half its heroes. Lu Zhishen passed away in seated meditation, Wu Song lost an arm, and many brothers fell in battle, died of illness or departed. Seven or eight out of every ten were gone. Though Song Jiang defeated and captured Fang La, the almost complete disappearance of his former companions filled him with grief beyond words as he brought the army home.

After the return, the court appointed Song Jiang Military Virtue Grand Master, Pacification Commissioner of Chuzhou and Chief Military Commander. He took up his post, governed well and earned the respect of soldiers and civilians alike. Yet treacherous ministers such as Cai Jing, Gao Qiu, Tong Guan and Yang Jian hated Liangshan's former outlaws and would not tolerate them. Forging an imperial order, they sent Song Jiang a gift of royal wine secretly laced with a slow poison. After drinking it, he realized that he must die. Fearing that Li Kui would rebel when he learned the truth and ruin the reputation for loyalty and righteousness that Song Jiang had built, he summoned Li Kui and shared the poisoned wine with him. Li Kui was buried at Liao'er Marsh in Chuzhou; Song Jiang, Wu Yong and Hua Rong also came to rest there. Even at his death, Song Jiang declared, "The court may betray me, but my loyal heart will never betray the court." His loyalty and righteousness remained unaltered to the end.

After Song Jiang's death, his spirit manifested its power. One night Emperor Huizong dreamed that he visited Liangshan Marsh and heard Song Jiang plead his grievance. Waking with a sigh, the emperor granted him the posthumous title of Loyal and Righteous Marquis of Spiritual Aid and Response, built a temple at Liao'er Marsh and ordered seasonal sacrifices. Moved by his loyalty, later generations kept the incense burning. Throughout his life, Song Jiang put righteousness first, gathered the heroes at Liangshan and carried out Heaven's will. His loyalty to the sovereign finally led him to submit to the court, yet after success he died at the hands of treacherous ministers. Readers close the book with a long sigh. The name Protector of Righteousness thus endures with those of Water Margin's 108 heroes.
宋江，字公明，郓城县宋家村人氏。其面黑身矮，人皆唤作「黑宋江」；又因平生仗义疏财.ja:
宋江、字は公明。鄆城県宋家村の出身である。顔が黒く背が低いため「黒宋江」と呼ばれた。また、生涯にわたって義を重んじ、財を惜しまず貧しい者や困窮する者を救ったため、その名は江湖に広まり、山東や河北で名を聞く者は皆敬服した。そこから「及時雨」という美称も得た。父母に孝を尽くしたので、郷里では孝義黒三郎とも称された。「呼保義」とは、国を守り民を安んずる義士を自ら名乗り、忠義の心を示したもので、このあだ名はそこに由来する。

宋江は初め鄆城県の押司を務め、文書の扱いに長け、役所の実務にも通じていた。さらに槍棒の稽古を好み、多くの武芸を学んだ。人柄は外柔内剛で、天下の豪傑と交わることを喜び、頼って来る者があれば身分の高低を問わず屋敷に留めてもてなした。旅立つ際には費用をすべて援助し、まさしく金を土のように使った。その恩義に感じた江湖の好漢は、皆彼のためなら死をも惜しまなかった。

宋江が梁山へ至るきっかけは、晁蓋をひそかに逃したことであった。晁蓋ら七人による生辰綱強奪が露見し、役所が捕り手を差し向けると、宋江はそれを知って夜を徹して知らせ、晁蓋を逃がして梁山へ走らせた。その後、妾の閻婆惜が梁山からの手紙を盾に宋江を脅した。宋江は怒りのあまり彼女を殺し、罪に問われ、刺青を入れられて江州へ流されることになった。道中、梁山や掲陽嶺などで多くの豪傑と知り合い、江州では戴宗、李逵と親交を結んだ。ある日、酒に酔って潯陽楼に謀反の詩を書きつけ、黄文炳に告発されて死罪となった。刑が執行される寸前、晁蓋が梁山の好漢を率いて刑場を襲い、宋江を救い出した。李逵も板斧を振るい、勢いに任せて斬りまくった。こうして初めて宋江は草莽に身を投じ、梁山へ登ったのである。

晁蓋は矢を受けて死ぬ際、史文恭を捕らえた者を山寨の主とするよう言い残した。のちに盧俊義が史文恭を捕らえたが、皆の推戴によって、結局宋江が第一の席に座り、梁山泊の総頭領となった。天魁星に位し、百八人の筆頭である。山寨では旗号を定め、職務を分け、忠義堂を建て、「替天行道」の杏黄色の大旗を掲げ、忠義をもって群雄に呼びかけた。武芸では林沖や関勝らに及ばなかったものの、恩情と信義、人徳で人々を従え、兵の配置に才を発揮し、帷幕の内で策を練った。三十六天罡と七十二地煞は心を合わせて力を尽くし、皆その号令を聞いた。祝家荘への三度の攻撃、連環馬の撃破、曾頭市攻略、童貫への二勝、高俅への三勝は、いずれも宋江が全体を指揮して成し遂げたものである。

宋江が生涯求めたのは草莽の暮らしではなく、招安であった。朝廷から刺配を受けた恩怨を思う一方、君に忠を尽くし国に報いる心を抱き、天子が早く招安の詔を下すことを願ってやまなかった。やがて宿太尉と燕青の働きかけで徽宗の心が変わり、朝廷は詔を発した。梁山泊の好漢は皆帰順した。招安後、宋江は軍を率いて大遼を征討し、遼軍を大破して殊勲を立てた。続いて河北の田虎、淮西の王慶の討伐を命じられ、いずれも勝利して帰還した。最後に方臘を討つため南征を命じられたが、この戦いは最も凄惨であった。江南の山河は険しく、方臘の兵力は大きく、梁山の好漢は半数以上を失った。魯智深は坐化し、武松は片腕を失い、多くの兄弟が戦死し、病没し、あるいは去っていった。十人のうち七、八人が失われたのである。宋江は方臘を平らげ、生け捕りにしたものの、帰途にはかつての豪傑がほとんど残っていないのを見て、言葉にできぬ悲しみに沈んだ。

凱旋後、朝廷は宋江を武徳大夫、楚州安撫使、兼兵馬都総管に任じた。任地での統治はよく、軍民の敬服を得た。しかし蔡京、高俅、童貫、楊戩ら奸臣は梁山の旧人を忌み嫌い、最後まで容れなかった。彼らは詔を偽り、御酒を賜ると称して、ひそかに遅効性の毒を混ぜた酒を宋江に送った。飲んだ宋江は、毒に当たり死を免れぬと悟った。そして李逵が事情を知って反乱を起こし、生涯の忠義の名を損なうことを恐れ、彼を呼び寄せて同じ毒酒を飲ませた。李逵は死後、楚州の蓼児窪に葬られ、宋江、呉用、花栄もこの地へ帰した。宋江は臨終にさえ、朝廷が自分を裏切っても、自分の忠心は朝廷を裏切らぬと嘆いた。その忠義が死に至るまで変わらなかったことがうかがえる。

宋江の死後、その霊は験を現した。徽宗はある夜、夢で梁山泊を訪れ、宋江が冤罪を訴えるのを見た。目覚めて嘆息し、宋江を忠烈義済霊応侯に封じ、蓼児窪に廟を建て、四季の祭祀を命じた。後世の人々もその忠義に感じ、香火を絶やさなかった。宋江は一生、義を第一とし、梁山に義士を集め、天に代わって道を行った。そして忠君の念から朝廷へ帰順したが、功を成しながら奸臣の手に命を落とした。読者が本を閉じて長く嘆くのもそのためである。呼保義の名は、水滸の百八人の好漢とともに不朽のものとなった。
宋江，字公明，郓城县宋家村人氏。其面黑身矮，人皆唤作「黑宋江」；又因平生仗义疏财.zh_TW:
宋江，字公明，鄆城縣宋家村人氏。其面黑身矮，人皆喚作「黑宋江」；又因平生仗義疏財，濟人貧苦，扶人之困，名聞江湖，山東、河北聞其名者無不敬服，故又得美號「及時雨」。其孝事父母，鄉里稱為孝義黑三郎。所謂「呼保義」者，自呼為保國安民之義士，以表忠義之心，此綽號之由來也。

宋江初為鄆城縣押司，刀筆精通，吏道純熟，更兼愛習槍棒，學得武藝多般。其為人外柔內剛，喜結天下豪傑，凡有投奔他者，無問高低，盡皆留在莊上款待，若要起身，盡數資助，端的揮金似土。江湖好漢感其恩義，皆願為其效死。

宋江上山之緣，起於私放晁蓋。晁蓋等七人智取生辰綱事發，官府差人捕拿，宋江得知，星夜報與晁蓋，使其得脫，投奔梁山。其後宋江因事殺了外室閻婆惜，惜以梁山書信要挾，宋江怒起，一時殺之，遂吃了官司，刺配江州。途經梁山、揭陽嶺等處，結識眾多豪傑。至江州，與戴宗、李逵相厚。一日酒醉，於潯陽樓題下反詩，為黃文炳所告，問成死罪。臨刑之際，晁蓋率梁山好漢劫了法場，救出宋江，又有李逵掄板斧殺得性起。自此宋江方才落草，上了梁山。

晁蓋中箭身死之後，遺言能擒史文恭者為山寨之主。後盧俊義擒得史文恭，然眾人推戴，宋江終坐第一把交椅，為梁山泊都頭領，居天魁星之位，梁山一百單八將之首。其在山寨，定旗號，分職事，立忠義堂，豎「替天行道」杏黃大旗，以忠義號召群雄。宋江雖武藝不及林沖、關勝諸將，然以恩信德義服眾，排程有方，運籌於帷幄，使三十六天罡、七十二地煞同心戮力，皆聽其號令。三打祝家莊、大破連環馬、攻打曾頭市、兩贏童貫、三敗高俅，宋江俱總其成。

宋江平生志向，不在草莽，而在招安。其每念身受朝廷刺配之恩怨，又懷忠君報國之心，常以「望天王降詔早招安」自期。後果借宿太尉、燕青說得徽宗迴心，朝廷頒詔，梁山泊眾好漢盡皆歸順。招安之後，宋江統軍征討大遼，大破遼兵，立下殊功。繼而奉命征剿河北田虎、淮西王慶，皆奏凱還。終又奉旨南征方臘。此一役最為慘烈，江南山川險惡，方臘兵勢浩大，梁山好漢折損過半，魯智深坐化，武松斷臂，諸多兄弟或陣亡，或病故，或離去，十去七八。宋江雖平了方臘，生擒方臘，然回師之時，但見昔日豪傑凋零殆盡，心中悲愴難言。

班師之後，朝廷封宋江為武德大夫、楚州安撫使，兼兵馬都總管。宋江赴任，撫治有方，軍民敬服。然奸臣蔡京、高俅、童貫、楊戩之輩忌恨梁山舊人，終不能容。彼等矯詔，賜御酒於宋江，酒中暗下慢藥。宋江飲罷，自知中毒必死，又恐李逵聞知反叛，壞了一世忠義之名，遂喚李逵至，與之同飲藥酒。李逵死後葬於楚州蓼兒窪。宋江與吳用、花榮亦俱歸此地。宋江臨終猶嘆「寧可朝廷負我，我忠心不負朝廷」，可見其忠義至死不渝。

宋江既死，神靈顯應。徽宗一夜夢遊梁山泊，見宋江訴冤，醒後嗟嘆，敕封宋江為忠烈義濟靈應侯，立廟蓼兒窪，四時祭享。後人感其忠義，香火不絕。宋江一生，仗義為先，聚義梁山，替天行道，終以忠君之念歸順朝廷，雖功成而身死奸佞之手，令讀者掩卷而長嘆焉。其呼保義之名，遂與水滸一百單八將同垂不朽。

宋清，绰号「铁扇子」，郓城县宋家村人氏，应地俊星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十六.en:
Song Qing, nicknamed Iron Fan, came from Song Family Village in Yuncheng County. He embodied the Earthly Star of Elegance and occupied the 76th seat among Liangshan Marsh's 108 heroes. As the younger brother of Song Jiang, Timely Rain, he held a distinctive position among the band and was the leader responsible for banquets, ceremonies and household affairs. Handsome and well mannered, he treated people with composed courtesy. The martial world gave him the refined name Iron Fan, suggesting an elegant gentleman holding an iron fan: gracious and thorough, he remained unhurried amid noisy feasts and complicated practical duties.

Song Qing and Song Jiang were the sons of Old Master Song, Jiang the elder and Qing the younger. Theirs was a prosperous farming household in Yuncheng County. Song Jiang worked as a county clerk, giving freely and befriending heroes everywhere, while Song Qing mostly stayed home to serve their father and manage the fields and household. He was dutiful, law-abiding and respectful toward his family. After Song Jiang secretly freed Chao Gai and killed Yan Poxi, he faced prosecution and fled into the martial world; Old Master Song and Song Qing remained in their village. Fearing that Song Jiang would become an outlaw and bring trouble upon the family, and also fearing legal reprisals, the old man devised a way to lure him home. Thus came the episode in which Song Jiang returned to visit his family, was arrested and was tattooed and exiled to Jiangzhou. Song Qing continued caring for his father and home throughout, rather than fleeing with his brother.

In Jiangzhou, Song Jiang nearly lost his life over a rebellious poem. Liangshan's heroes rescued him from the execution ground, after which he joined them on the mountain. Chao Gai and Song Jiang subsequently made repeated efforts to bring Old Master Song and Song Qing there as well, sparing them the danger of prosecution in their village. Song Qing then lived at Liangshan with his father and brother and became part of its community. He was neither a fierce front-line warrior nor a strategist planning in the command tent. Yet he was steady and dependable, so Song Jiang entrusted him with feasts, celebrations and the reception and farewell of guests. Song Qing arranged every large and small banquet, reward feast for the troops and reception of visitors, keeping everything orderly and pleasing hosts and guests alike. Among those fierce woodland outlaws, such a courteous, considerate man was like an iron fan that tempered the atmosphere. He maintained the mountain's dignity in manners and social dealings, performing a quiet but valuable duty.

At the great assembly and ranking of Liangshan's heroes, Song Qing took the 76th seat as the Earthly Star of Elegance, with sole responsibility for banquets. Both his star and the name Iron Fan reflected his refinement, good looks and skill in practical affairs. Though he never won spectacular glory by slaying generals or seizing banners, his place as Song Jiang's brother and his ability to organize feasts and receive guests made him indispensable to Liangshan's domestic arrangements and ceremonies. After the court granted amnesty, he followed Song Jiang's army north against the Liao, then against Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi, and finally south against Fang La in Jiangnan. Throughout these campaigns he stayed by his brother, managing army affairs. He escaped death in battle and preserved his life, becoming one of the few Liangshan heroes to reach a peaceful end.

After Fang La's defeat and the army's return, the court rewarded the commanders according to their merits, and Song Qing too received an official appointment. By then Old Master Song had died. As a son grieving his father, and having seen almost all Liangshan's brothers killed, wounded or scattered, Song Qing no longer desired fame or official life. Unwilling to enter the turmoil of court politics, he submitted his resignation, pleaded illness and returned to Song Family Village in Yuncheng County. There he resumed farming, preserved the ancestral property, worked the fields and spent his remaining years in peace. Later Song Jiang died in Chuzhou, poisoned by treacherous ministers. Though Song Qing could not be at his side, he himself was able to grow old in his native village, unlike so many brothers who returned wrapped in horsehide or died far from home. Iron Fan was never famed for martial courage. Filial devotion, kindness and the wisdom to know when to stop defined him. Beginning in Song Family Village and returning there at the end, he withdrew unharmed from the rise and dispersal of Liangshan's 108 and lived out his days at home: an uncommon conclusion to a hero's story.
宋清，绰号「铁扇子」，郓城县宋家村人氏，应地俊星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十六.ja:
宋清は「鉄扇子」と呼ばれ、鄆城県宋家村の出身である。地俊星に応じ、梁山泊百八人のうち第七十六位に座した。及時雨・宋江の実の弟という、好漢たちの中でも特別な立場にあり、宴席や儀礼、庶務を専門に取り仕切る頭領であった。容姿は端正で、振る舞いは温雅、人との応対にも落ち着きと節度があった。江湖で贈られた「鉄扇子」という雅号は、鉄の扇を手にした風雅な士のように、物腰が優れ、万事に配慮が届くことをいう。騒がしい宴や入り組んだ雑務の中でも、慌てぬ気品を保つ人物であった。

宋清と宋江はともに宋太公の子で、宋江が兄、宋清が弟である。もとは鄆城県の裕福な農家であった。宋江は県の押司を務め、義を重んじて財を惜しまず、天下の豪傑と交わった。一方の宋清は、主に家にいて老父に仕え、田畑と家事を切り盛りする、分を守った孝行で慎み深い男であった。宋江は晁蓋をひそかに逃し、さらに閻婆惜を殺したため罪に問われ、江湖へ逃れたが、宋太公と宋清は宋家村に残った。のちに父は、宋江が外で山賊となって家を巻き込むことを恐れ、また罪が一族に及ぶことも案じて、彼を計略で呼び戻した。これが、宋江が帰郷して親を訪ね、官府に捕らえられ、刺配されて江州へ送られる一節につながる。宋清は終始、家で老父を守り、戸口を預かり、兄とともに逃亡することはなかった。

江州へ流された宋江は、謀反の詩によってまたも命を失いかけたが、梁山の好漢が刑場を襲って救い出し、ついに梁山へ登った。その後、晁蓋と宋江は幾度も手を尽くし、宋太公と宋清も山へ迎え、郷里に残って役所の追及に苦しむことのないようにした。以来、宋清は父兄と梁山泊に住み、その一員となった。敵陣へ突き進む猛将でも、帷幕で策を練る軍師でもなかったが、落ち着いた人柄と手際のよさを買われ、山寨の宴会、慶事、来客の出迎えや見送りを宋江から任された。大小の宴、将兵への慰労、客の接待はすべて彼が整え、秩序よく運んで主客を楽しませた。殺気立つ緑林の好漢たちの中で、宋清のように温雅で行き届いた人物は、場の空気を和らげる鉄の扇にも似ていた。山寨の礼節と人情の体面を保つ、得難く堅実な役目であった。

梁山の大集会で英雄の席次が定まると、宋清は第七十六位、地俊星となり、宴席を専門に管理した。「地俊」の星名も「鉄扇子」のあだ名も、その温雅で秀麗な姿と庶務への適性を表している。戦場で敵将を斬り旗を奪う赫々たる戦功こそなかったが、宋江の弟として、また宴と接客の才を持つ者として、梁山の内務と儀礼に欠かせない位置を占めた。朝廷の招安を受けたのちは、宋江の大軍に従って北の遼を征し、勅命で河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を討ち、さらに南下して江南の方臘を征討した。転戦する間も常に兄のそばに仕え、軍中の雑務を切り盛りした。刀兵の災いには遭わず命を保ち、梁山の好漢では数少ない、穏やかな最期を得る一人となった。

方臘を平定して凱旋すると、朝廷は功を論じて諸将に褒賞を与え、宋清にも官職を授けた。しかしそのころ、兄弟の父・宋太公はすでに亡くなっていた。宋清は子として父を思い、また梁山の兄弟が死傷し、離散して、わずかしか残っていないのを見て、功名や仕官への望みを失っていた。官界の波乱に再び関わることを嫌い、辞官の上表をし、病を理由に故郷へ帰った。鄆城県宋家村で再び農家となり、祖業を守って自ら田畑を耕し、余生を安らかに送った。のちに宋江は楚州で奸臣の毒酒によって死んだ。宋清はそのそばにはいられなかったが、多くの兄弟のように戦死して異郷の土となることなく、自らは故郷で天寿を全うできた。鉄扇子・宋清は、生涯、武勇で名を立てず、孝悌と温厚さ、退くべき時を知る賢さによって身を処した。宋家村から出て宋家村へ帰り、梁山百八人の盛衰と離合集散の中で、無事に身を引き郷里で寿命を終えた。これもまた、ありきたりではない好漢の結末である。
宋清，绰号「铁扇子」，郓城县宋家村人氏，应地俊星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十六.zh_TW:
宋清，綽號「鐵扇子」，鄆城縣宋家村人氏，應地俊星，於梁山泊一百單八將中坐第七十六把交椅。他乃及時雨宋江的親兄弟，論身份在梁山眾好漢中頗為特殊，是頭領之中專司宴飲筵席、禮儀庶務的一位。其人生得儀表端正、舉止溫文，待人接物從容有度，江湖上送他一個雅號喚作「鐵扇子」，言其風度翩翩、處事周全，如手執鐵扇的雅士，於喧騰筵宴、紛繁庶務之間，自有一段從容不迫的氣度。

宋清與宋江同是宋太公膝下之子，宋江居長，宋清為弟，本是鄆城縣一戶殷實莊戶人家。宋江在縣中做押司，仗義疏財，結交天下豪傑，宋清則多在家中侍奉老父宋太公，操持田園家務，是個安分守己、孝悌端謹的人物。宋江因私放晁蓋、又殺了閻婆惜，吃了官司，亡命江湖，宋太公與宋清留在宋家村。後宋太公恐宋江在外落草、連累家門，又怕官司株連，曾設法將宋江賺回，乃有「宋江回鄉省親、被官府緝拿刺配江州」一節，宋清在家中始終守著老父，照看門戶，未曾與兄長一同亡命。

宋江刺配江州、又因題反詩幾乎喪命，得梁山好漢劫法場相救，遂上了梁山。其後晁蓋、宋江數次設法，將宋太公與宋清一併接上山來，免得留在鄉中受官司之苦。宋清自此隨父兄同居梁山泊，成為梁山一脈。他既非衝鋒陷陣的猛將，亦非運籌帷幄的謀士，然其為人穩重、辦事妥帖，宋江便委他執掌山寨中筵宴慶賀、接待迎送之務。凡梁山大小宴會、犒賞將士、招待來賓，皆由宋清一手張羅，安排得井井有條、賓主盡歡。在那一班殺氣騰騰的綠林好漢之間，宋清這般溫文周到的人物，恰似一柄調和氣氛的鐵扇，使山寨的禮數人情不致失了體面，亦是一份難得的穩妥差事。

梁山大聚義、英雄排座次，宋清名列第七十六位，應地俊星，專一掌管筵宴。這「地俊」之號與「鐵扇子」之綽，皆見其溫雅俊秀、長於庶務的本色。他雖不曾在沙場上斬將搴旗、立下赫赫戰功，卻以宋江之弟的身份、以掌宴待客之能，在梁山的內務禮儀中佔著一席不可或缺之地。後梁山受朝廷招安，宋清隨宋江大軍北征遼國，又奉旨剿討河北田虎、淮西王慶，再南下征討江南方臘，一路轉戰，始終隨侍兄長左右，操持軍中庶務，未曾陷於刀兵之厄，得以保全性命，乃是梁山好漢中難得善終的一位。

平定方臘、班師還朝之後，朝廷論功行賞，封賞諸將。宋清亦得蒙封賜官職。然其時宋江、宋清的老父宋太公已然亡故，宋清身為人子，又眼見梁山弟兄死傷離散、所餘無幾，已無心於功名宦海。他不願再涉官場風波，遂上表辭官，告病還鄉，回到鄆城縣宋家村，重做一個莊家田戶，奉守祖業、躬耕隴畝，安享餘年。後宋江在楚州遭奸臣以鴆酒毒害身亡，宋清雖未能在側，卻也得以在故鄉終老，不曾如眾多弟兄那般馬革裹屍、客死他鄉。這鐵扇子宋清，平生不以武勇顯名，卻以孝悌溫厚、明哲知止立身，自宋家村起、復歸宋家村終，於梁山一百單八人風雲聚散之中，落了個全身而退、壽終鄉里的結局，亦是一段不落俗套的好漢收梢。

宋万者,梁山泊开山元老之一也。其籍贯出身,原著不甚详载,只知他生得身材高大,凛凛.en:
Song Wan was one of Liangshan Marsh's founding veterans. The original tale gives little detail about his birthplace or early life; it tells us only that he was a tall, imposing man, known in the martial world as Vajra in the Clouds. The name vividly describes his enormous frame.
